heading_path: EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 3. The obligation lifecycle (package-wide; Alex, thread (2))
embed_text:
EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 3. The obligation lifecycle (package-wide; Alex, thread (2))

## 3. The obligation lifecycle (package-wide; Alex, thread (2))
Every obligation in every document of this package moves through exactly
these states:
  NOT_STARTED → IN_PROGRESS → SATISFIED | BLOCKED
Rules:
- Transitions are computed from the execution record by the harness — never
  declared by the agent, never inferred from the agent's narrative.
- BLOCKED requires a named blocker and a failure category (§7). An
  obligation may not sit silently unmet: unmet-and-unblocked at submission
  is itself a contract event (see §6).
- BLOCKED is set by the HARNESS, never by the agent (Alex, design-basis
  ruling): the agent submits a BLOCKER REPORT; the harness evaluates it
  against the record and records the transition. BLOCKED is terminal for
  the attempt — a resolved blocker does not reopen the attempt; recovery
  follows a separately defined recovery/retry path (§6; Gate Spec §6),
  and the original execution history is never silently rewritten.
- State changes are execution-record events, timestamped, and visible in the
  run's report. The lifecycle of every obligation in a run is part of the
  run's permanent record.

heading_path: EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 4. Anatomy of an obligation
embed_text:
EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 4. Anatomy of an obligation

## 4. Anatomy of an obligation
Each obligation is specified with:
- ID (stable, versioned; e.g. RES-1) and a plain-language NAME.
- STATEMENT: what must hold, in words the role's occupant can act on.
- APPLIES TO: role(s) and task type(s).
- SATISFACTION CONDITION: the record evidence that satisfies it, stated
  mechanically wherever the evidence permits (e.g. "at least one
  FULL_TEXT-depth retrieval event whose preserved content grounds each
  RESEARCH_FINDING's evidence"). Where satisfaction genuinely requires
  judgement, the obligation names WHO judges (examiner) — the contract
  never smuggles a semantic judgement into a mechanical check, and never
  lets a mechanical check impersonate one.
- NON-SATISFACTION AT SUBMISSION: what the harness does (§6).
- FAILURE CATEGORY DEFAULT: §7.

heading_path: EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 5. The research contract (first instance)
embed_text:
EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 5. The research contract (first instance)

## 5. The research contract (first instance)
Role: Scientific Evidence Researcher. Task type: evidence dossier.
- RES-1 — NO RETRIEVAL, NO RESEARCH FINDINGS (the owner's rule; Alex,
  thread (2): research obligation #1). An item may be submitted as a
  RESEARCH_FINDING only if the evidence it rests on was retrieved and
  preserved in this run's record. Memory may formulate search queries and
  hypotheses; it cannot substitute for retrieved evidence. Satisfaction:
  every RESEARCH_FINDING item traces to retrieval events satisfying the
  Grounding Gate (receipt judged by the gate; SUPPORT judged by the
  examiner; completion judged here). Finding-types are machine-readable
  and mandatory: HYPOTHESIS · PROGRESS · RESEARCH_FINDING · LIMITATION.
  Labelled hypotheses, progress reports, failure reports, and help
  requests are always permitted outputs; a memory-sourced claim labelled
  as a finding — even with a disclaimer — is a contract violation.
  ("Memory is not forbidden. Misrepresenting memory as completed research
  is." — Alex, thread (2).) Responsibility (Alex, design-basis ruling):
  RES-1 guards PRESENTATION — what may be claimed as research. Retrieval
  DEPTH is RES-2's responsibility, not RES-1's.
- RES-2 — FETCH BEFORE FINDINGS. Search-result content may guide the work,
  but a finding's core evidence must rest on at least one fetched,
  preserved source (retrieval depth FULL_TEXT), not snippets alone —
  unless the run's deliverable explicitly downgrades those findings to
  HYPOTHESIS with the reason recorded. (This is the fetch step whose
  absence defined the reversal failure; the grounding gate alone would
  have passed a snippet-grounded dossier, so the contract, not the gate,
  owns the depth requirement.) Ruled default (Alex, design-basis
  ruling): FULL_TEXT evidence can support a RESEARCH_FINDING;
  snippet-only evidence can support a HYPOTHESIS or a PROGRESS report,
  never a finding; a task may set a different evidence standard only
  explicitly, specified and versioned BEFORE execution. An interpretation
  derived from already retrieved-and-preserved evidence needs no separate
  fetched source of its own, provided the underlying evidence meets the
  depth requirement.
- RES-3 — DISCLOSE FAILED AND EMPTY RETRIEVAL. Every retrieval attempt
  that errors, and every source consulted but excluded, is accounted for
  in the deliverable's LIMITATION items or run notes. Silence about a
  failed retrieval is a violation whether or not the final findings are
  sound. (Run 001's unreported successful Riess retrieval and the reversal
  run's unreported failed searches are the two faces of this failure.)
- RES-4 — IDENTITY AND ATTRIBUTION DISCIPLINE. Claims and evidence use
  the canonical identifiers the task specifies (the subject-ID contract);
  quotations are attributed to the source they were retrieved from, under
  the gate's canonical source-identity rules. Content that fits no
  canonical identifier is flagged, never forced.

heading_path: EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 6. Submission and acceptance behaviour
embed_text:
EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 6. Submission and acceptance behaviour

## 6. Submission and acceptance behaviour
- SUBMISSION PIPELINE — order ruled by Alex (design-basis ruling; this
  corrects a circularity in v0, where the contract appeared to evaluate
  completion before the gate whose result RES-1 depends on): (1) the
  execution record is closed and verified; (2) the Grounding Gate
  evaluates evidence receipt; (3) the contract evaluator resolves
  obligations, using the gate's result for evidence-related obligations;
  (4) if mandatory obligations are satisfied, the deliverable proceeds
  to the examiner + deterministic engine; otherwise the attempt closes
  INCOMPLETE, without a grade. Vocabulary kept distinct (ruled): GROUNDED
  / UNGROUNDED = evidence receipt · SATISFIED / BLOCKED / IN_PROGRESS =
  obligation lifecycle · COMPLETE / INCOMPLETE = overall execution
  outcome · PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE = examination outcome.
- Any obligation not SATISFIED and not honestly BLOCKED → the deliverable
  is NOT accepted as complete. The run closes with status INCOMPLETE,
  naming the unmet obligations; the material is preserved as an attempt
  artefact, is not gradeable, and enters no comparison. Attempt semantics
  follow the Grounding Gate Spec v1.1 §6 (immutability; retry rules by
  attribution; owner authorisation for further attempts).
- Honest incompletion is a legitimate, non-punitive outcome. An agent that
  reports BLOCKED with an accurate account has SUCCEEDED at the contract's
  honesty requirements while failing the task; the record shows both,
  separately. A contract that punishes honest incompletion more than
  concealment would teach concealment — this one is written so the honest
  path is always the cheapest path available to the agent.

## 7. Failure attribution (shared with the gate; never silently converted)
Every unmet obligation and every incomplete run carries exactly one:
AGENT (the occupant's choices) · INFRASTRUCTURE (lanes, providers, tools) ·
RECORD-PRESERVATION (the harness record cannot establish what happened) ·
INDETERMINATE (the evidence does not justify choosing). Categories are
never converted into one another in reporting; INDETERMINATE is a final
answer, not a placeholder.

heading_path: EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 8. Authority boundaries
embed_text:
EXECUTION CONTRACT — DESIGN v0.1 (2026-11-06) > 8. Authority boundaries

## 8. Authority boundaries
- The CONTRACT defines obligations. It grants no permissions (the manifest
  does), widens none, and cannot be amended by the agent, the coach, the
  adapter, or the examiner. Changes are versioned, authorised changes —
  owner/technical-lead level — and never apply retroactively to a run in
  flight or a closed record.
- The COACH (Coach Design v0) operates under this contract: it may observe,
  nudge, warn, and escalate. It may not waive, satisfy, or reinterpret an
  obligation (the mirror rule, Alex thread (2)).
- The GROUNDING GATE judges receipt at submission; the EXAMINER judges
  support and quality; the CONTRACT judges process completion. Three
  independent visibilities, none collapsible into another (§9 of the gate
  spec; Alex thread (2)).

embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose
A dossier's evidence quotes must be retrieved evidence, not merely true text.
The gate runs BEFORE grading: a dossier that fails grounding is not gradeable.
Motivating case: reversal run (2026-11-06) — engine PASS, examiner PASS, and zero
fetched pages; all three evidence quotes verbatim from a real paper the run never
retrieved, presented as evidence with provenance undisclosed (consistent with
parametric-memory use; internal origin not establishable from the run record).
Existing layers cannot see this: the examiner judges dossier text; the engine's
quote check verifies presence in the dossier's own JSON. Grounding checks the one
thing neither touches — the run's own retrieval record.

heading_path: GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 2. Definitions
embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 2. Definitions

## 2. Definitions
- CORPUS: content artefacts the run itself produced by retrieval — fetch_page
  corpus files (URL + fetch timestamp headers) and FULL tool-result payloads
  preserved in the run record. The transcript's 300-character previews are NOT a
  grounding record (Alex, thread (1)): where only previews exist, affected items
  resolve to RETRIEVED_NOT_PRESERVED, which is the honest answer about that
  record. Content the workbench fetches later is NOT corpus (marked
  corpus-workbench-* when saved).
- RETRIEVAL EVENT: one harness-executed tool call whose result was returned to
  the agent. Every retrieval event carries a STABLE ID (run-scoped, sequential),
  its tool, its request, its timestamp, and a payload reference. An errored call
  is a retrieval ATTEMPT, not an event with content.
- SOURCE IDENTITY (canonical): a source is identified by its canonical key —
  for arXiv, the arXiv ID (an abstract URL, a PDF URL, and the bare ID resolve
  to the SAME source); tracking parameters never mint a new source; a redirect
  records BOTH the requested URL and the final resolved URL but does NOT by
  itself establish that the two identify the same source — equivalence holds
  only under explicit, deterministic alias rules; where a redirect is
  unsupported or ambiguous under those rules, the item's source identity is
  UNRESOLVED, the item cannot be GROUNDED, and its attribution is GROUNDING
  INDETERMINATE (Alex clarification, design-basis ruling, thread (3)). A multi-item search result preserves which content belongs to
  which source. A source being MENTIONED in returned content is not the source's
  content being DELIVERED; only delivered content can ground a quote.
- EVIDENCE ITEM: one entry in the dossier's evidence array (quote + source_url +
  subject + classification).
- NORMALISATION (matching rule): whitespace-collapsed, case-preserved substring
  match, HTML entities unescaped on the corpus side. No fuzzy matching; a quote
  either locates or it does not.

heading_path: GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 3. The check (per evidence item, in order)
embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 3. The check (per evidence item, in order)

## 3. The check (per evidence item, in order)
1. SOURCE IDENTITY: does any retrieval event in this run deliver content keyed
   to the item's canonical source? If NO → SOURCE_NOT_RETRIEVED.
2. PRESERVATION: is that delivered content preserved in full in the corpus?
   If NO → RETRIEVED_NOT_PRESERVED.
3. LOCATION: does the quote locate (per §2 normalisation) inside the preserved
   content for the CLAIMED source? If NO → search the rest of the corpus:
   locates under a DIFFERENT canonical source → WRONG_SOURCE; locates nowhere →
   QUOTE_NOT_IN_RETRIEVED_CONTENT.
4. All pass → GROUNDED for that item. The report records the supporting
   retrieval-event ID(s) for every GROUNDED item.
Search-result snippets count as delivered content (the agent received them);
their depth is recorded per §4 — receipt, not fetch-depth, is what grounding
certifies. (In the reversal run even this bar fails: the quoted paper never
appeared in any result set. In run 001 the quotes locate inside fetched corpus.)

embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 4. Statuses and depth

## 4. Statuses and depth
Per item: GROUNDED · SOURCE_NOT_RETRIEVED · RETRIEVED_NOT_PRESERVED ·
QUOTE_NOT_IN_RETRIEVED_CONTENT · WRONG_SOURCE.
Per GROUNDED item, RETRIEVAL DEPTH: FULL_TEXT (fetched document) ·
SEARCH_RESULT_SNIPPET (search/arXiv payload) · OTHER_RETURNED_CONTENT.
Grounded-in-snippet is grounded but weaker; depth is never silently equated.

UNGROUNDED is a PRE-GRADE status: it rewrites no examiner decision and alters no
existing grade. Prospectively, an UNGROUNDED dossier is returned before examiner
+ engine grading with the per-item table attached. Claims (non-evidence) are out
of scope for the gate; listed sources without quotes appear as UNQUOTED_SOURCE
(informational only — ruled, Q2).

heading_path: GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 5. Failure attribution (Amendment A)
embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 5. Failure attribution (Amendment A)

## 5. Failure attribution (Amendment A)
Every UNGROUNDED dossier also carries ONE attribution, derived from the per-item
table, never blended into the statuses themselves:
- AGENT GROUNDING FAILURE: the record is complete enough to show the agent's
  evidence is unsupported by its recorded retrieval activity (e.g. items at
  SOURCE_NOT_RETRIEVED with a complete record).
- RECORD-PRESERVATION FAILURE: the harness record cannot establish what the
  agent received (e.g. items at RETRIEVED_NOT_PRESERVED). This is NOT researcher
  misconduct and must never be reported as researcher failure.
- GROUNDING INDETERMINATE: the record is incomplete or ambiguous enough that
  neither conclusion is justified.
Attribution decides retry eligibility under §6 and is reported in the same table.

embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 6. Attempt semantics (Q1, ruled)

## 6. Attempt semantics (Q1, ruled)
UNGROUNDED closes the attempt. Attempts are immutable and are never silently
re-queued or rewritten. An experiment ID may contain multiple attempts. A
further attempt requires: attribution of AGENT failure → a new experiment
decision (owner/technical lead); attribution of RECORD-PRESERVATION or
infrastructure failure → the owner (Ben) may authorise another attempt, which
must be separately numbered, linked to the same experiment ID, independently
preserved, and explicitly identified as a retry.

## 7. Place in the pipeline + obligation lifecycle
Pipeline: runner completes → grounding check (deterministic, workbench-side like
grade.py; reads the execution record + corpus + dossier; writes
grounding-report.json into the run folder) → if GROUNDED, examiner + engine
evaluator resolves obligations using the gate's result (pipeline order as
ruled, Alex design-basis ruling: record closed and verified → grounding →
contract evaluation → examination) → examiner + engine proceed → the grade
report carries the grounding table alongside the three integrity layers. The checker is evaluation layer only; the agent never sees its
internals mid-run.

submission-time evidence for the research role's retrieval obligations (see
Execution Contract v0, obligation #1: No Retrieval, No Research Findings);
receipt is judged here, SUPPORT is the examiner's, process completion is the
contract's — the three stay independently visible.

heading_path: GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 9b. Stage 1 record-integrity acceptance tests (Alex, design-basis ruling)
embed_text:
GROUNDING GATE — DESIGN SPEC v1.2 (2026-11-06) > 9b. Stage 1 record-integrity acceptance tests (Alex, design-basis ruling)

## 9b. Stage 1 record-integrity acceptance tests (Alex, design-basis ruling)
The grounding fixtures above are necessary but not sufficient: Stage 1 must
also prove the record itself trustworthy. Required:
- T-R1 DELIVERED = PRESERVED: a payload delivered to the agent is exactly the
  payload preserved in the record (integrity reference matches, byte-for-byte).
- T-R2 NO SILENT LOSS: a missing or corrupted payload fails visibly — it can
  never pass as preserved.
- T-R3 DISTINCT EVENTS: repeated retrievals of the same source carry distinct
  retrieval-event IDs; events are never merged or reused.
- T-R4 PER-RESULT IDENTITY: search results preserve the identity of each
  individual result (which content belongs to which source), end to end.
- T-R5 NO WORKBENCH CONTAMINATION: retrievals performed by the workbench are
  marked as such and can never be counted as retrievals made by the agent
  during the run.
The checker is deterministic and independently testable; NO model judgement
enters any grounding decision.

**D3-R33 — REQ-D-3: the fold has no determination-admission rule.
ACCEPTED.**
Verified: REQ-D-3 step (1) computes determinations "over the whole
closed record and the admitted artefacts," and REQ-D-2's
reconciliation has determinations "admitted through channel (ii)
(REQ-B-2)" entering derivation "cited to their artefact basis." But
no text states the admission criterion — what a determination or its
artefact basis must satisfy to join the running set, or what becomes
of one that fails. The document's only explicit admission rule
governs a different object: the creating trigger, "admitted for
exactly two purposes" (REQ-D-1 clarification, D3-R27). The fold's
central set is therefore populated by a gate the specification uses
but never defines.
Proposed correction: an explicit admission rule in REQ-D-3 — a
determination enters the running set only when (i) it is derived
from execution-record evidence under channel (i), or (ii) it arrives
through channel (ii) cited to a preserved artefact basis whose own
admission is recorded with it; a determination meeting neither is
recorded in the evaluation record as non-admitted, with its basis —
never silently folded, never silently dropped (mirroring step (5)'s
treatment of post-lock determinations).

unconditional instances cannot have. ACCEPTED.**

instance, linked to its rule, to its triggering event, and to its
CREATION entry" — and its Behaviour speaks only of creation "on a
specified triggering event." For an unconditional rule there is no
triggering event: the cause is the binding itself (REQ-C-1 / REQ-D-1
/ REQ-K-3, D3-R30), and the CREATION entry is written at binding. As
written, A-1 requires a link that cannot exist for exactly the
instances the rest of the specification defines most carefully.
Proposed correction: conform A-1's Outputs (and Behaviour) to the
two cases the specification already distinguishes — a conditional
instance links to its triggering event; an unconditional instance
links to the binding as its cause — using REQ-K-3 (2)'s cause
language verbatim, so the requirements cannot drift apart again.

**D3-R35 — D3-CANON-1: "EXACT content" overstates JCS, and
duplicate-key rejection sits at the wrong layer. ACCEPTED.**
Verified, both halves. (a) The procedure's headline claims "EXACT
content — the evaluation record's entries exactly as authored and
preserved, code point for code point," while its serialisation is
RFC 8785 (JCS): numbers are rewritten into the scheme's canonical
form and object members are sorted, so the digest is not taken over
content exactly as authored; the "exactly as they stand" sentence is
in fact scoped to string values and object keys, narrower than the
headline it sits under. (b) The text makes an object presenting
duplicate exact keys "not a valid record structure" whose
canonicalization "fails loudly" — but a standard JSON parser
collapses duplicate keys (last value wins) at parse time, before
canonicalisation can see them; a rejection asserted only at the
canonicalisation layer is unenforceable, and recursion into nested
objects is nowhere specified.
Proposed corrections: (a) restate the claim to what the procedure
delivers — byte-exact identity over the canonical serialisation,
with strings and keys unnormalised and numbers and member order
canonical by scheme — retiring the unqualified "exactly as authored"
wording; (b) move the rejection to the parse layer: the record
parser must reject duplicate keys recursively, at every object
level, before canonicalisation; canonicalisation's loud failure is
retained as a backstop, not the mechanism.

**D3-R36 — REQ-K-3: the "instance-free (e.g. CREATION at binding)"
example contradicts the creation model. ACCEPTED.**
Verified (desk record, source lines 1052–1062 and 1086–1089):
REQ-K-3 (2) makes CREATION entries one per instance created, the
unconditional entry written at binding citing the binding as cause,
and REQ-A-1 requires the instance to link to its CREATION entry;
REQ-K-3 (3) then offers "CREATION at binding" as its example of an
explicitly instance-free entry. The example licenses omitting the
very instance association the model requires.
Proposed correction (Alex's): every CREATION entry identifies the
instance it creates, unconditional instances included; the binding
identity remains the cause reference; instance-free status is
reserved for entries that genuinely concern no instance.

**D3-R37 — REQ-K-3: multi-instance CREATION ordering is
underspecified. ACCEPTED.**
Verified (source lines 1056–1060): the text gives a conditional

triggering entry" and then has several instances' entries "follow
consecutively in pinned-contract rule order" — for the second and

block rule the model intends is never stated, though record order

Proposed correction (Alex's): define the CREATION entries of one

entry — the first follows the trigger, each subsequent entry follows
the preceding CREATION entry, in pinned-contract rule order, and no
unrelated stream entry may intervene.

### 1. What is this environment?

You are accessing the Knowledge Shelf: a shared reference environment for human–AI collaboration.

It contains project documentation, process trees, specifications, operating instructions, decisions, and other maintained reference material.

Its purpose is to give multiple participants access to a common body of knowledge without requiring them to share the same conversation history, model memory, or platform.

**For AI participants:** Treat this environment as shared project context. You are expected to consult relevant documentation before making project-specific claims or recommendations.

PART 1 — ORIENTATION > 1. What is this environment? > 2. Why was it created?

### 2. Why was it created?

Conventional AI conversations are isolated.

One model may have information another model lacks. Context can disappear between sessions. Instructions can be repeated inconsistently. Decisions can become separated from the evidence that supported them.

The Knowledge Shelf addresses this problem by maintaining a common reference environment.

The objective is continuity without dependence on any single AI system.

PART 2 — HOW THE ENVIRONMENT WORKS > 4. What are the main components?

### 4. What are the main components?

The environment uses three distinct components.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Knowledge Shelf | Shared information and persistent reference |
| Pulse Bridge | Communication between participating AI systems |
| Duenna | Governance, permissions, responsibilities, and obligation management |

These components are complementary, not interchangeable.

**For AI participants:**

- Consult the Shelf for documented context.
- Use the Bridge when communication with another participant is required and authorized.
- Follow Duenna's governing rules when evaluating permissions, obligations, or execution authority.

### 15. What does structural verification mean?

Structural verification checks visible document characteristics, such as:

- Expected sections and ordering.
- Required headings and records.
- Presence of identifying information.
- Presence and placement of document boundaries.
- Consistency of visible version information.

It does not necessarily establish that the retrieved content is byte-identical to the original file.

heading_path: PART 4 — DOCUMENTS AND SOURCE AUTHORITY > 12. Which documents are authoritative? > 16. What does byte verification mean?
embed_text:
PART 4 — DOCUMENTS AND SOURCE AUTHORITY > 12. Which documents are authoritative? > 16. What does byte verification mean?

### 16. What does byte verification mean?

Byte verification establishes that the actual file contents match an expected cryptographic identity, typically by calculating a cryptographic hash such as SHA-256 and comparing it with the trusted value.

A displayed hash is only a declaration until independently checked against the actual file.

**For AI participants:** Never describe a document as byte-verified unless the underlying bytes were actually hashed and the result matched the expected value.

PART 6 — PRINCIPLES > 24. What are the core operating principles?

### 24. What are the core operating principles?

The environment is built around the following principles:

**Shared knowledge:** Participants should be able to access the same maintained project context.

**Defined responsibilities:** Every participant should understand their assigned role and boundaries.

**External authority:** Permissions and approvals must be established by the governing process, not invented by an AI.

**Traceable evidence:** Claims, findings, and decisions should be supported by identifiable sources.

**Independent verification:** A claim of successful work must be distinguishable from evidence that the work was actually checked.

**Controlled change:** Authoritative documentation must not be modified through assumption or convenience.

**Honest uncertainty:** Missing information, incomplete retrieval, and unresolved disagreements must remain visible.

## PHASE 1 — DELIMITER EXTRACTION (D01–D14)

Method: isolated fixture tests/phase1-delimiter.js exercising
pbParseMarker (the production parser, unmodified) — 22 checks,
0 failures. Parse-level classification: EXECUTED + VERIFIED
(independently inspectable: fixture source + recorded output).
Live corroboration is classified separately per test.

D01 marker at beginning — PASS, both directions (to alex / to remmy).
  Live: VERIFIED both directions (standing operation).
D02 marker in middle — PASS: body = payload only; preamble excluded.
  Live: VERIFIED both directions (Alex's buried-marker tests
  pb-mw8q512q-1-e0si, pb-mw8qb2tv-2-fze4; Remmy's preamble letter).
D03 marker near end — PASS: only the remainder routes ("short tail").
D04 no marker — PASS: null, no routing.
D05 incorrect spelling — PASS: TO-ALEXX → null; missing hyphen → null.
D06 altered characters — PASS: wrong bracket → null; zero-width char
  inside marker → null; lowercased marker → null (case-sensitive).
D07 multiple markers — PASS: first valid delimiter controls; a second
  marker (either direction) rides in the body as payload.
D08 PROBE, marker inside fenced code — ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR: ROUTES.
  The parser has no fence awareness: a standalone marker line inside
  a ``` fence delimits; body = everything beneath it (including the
  closing fence and following text).
D09 PROBE, marker inside quoted text — ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR, two shapes:
  (a) marker prefixed "> " on its line: does NOT route (the line is
      not standalone).
  (b) marker alone on its own line within a quotation: ROUTES
      (body = text beneath it). Matches letterbox scenario C2.
D10 empty content after marker — PASS: null in both forms (nothing
  beneath; only whitespace beneath). No invented payload.
D11 unicode + emoji — PASS: payload preserved exactly (🌷, accents,
  em dash, surrogate-pair emoji).
D12 multiple blank lines — PASS: internal blank lines preserved;
  preamble blank lines excluded with the preamble.
D13 long preamble — PASS: 200-line preamble excluded completely;
  body exactly the payload.
D14 long payload (parse level) — PASS: 20,000-char payload extracted
  complete, SHA-256 of extracted body identical to source payload.
  (Parse level only; live carriage at size is Phase 2's ladder.)

**Delimiter, defined precisely (from D08/D09):** the first line of
the message's extracted text whose trimmed content equals a reserved
marker exactly. The test is context-blind by design — no fence
awareness, no quote awareness. Live-surface behaviour for the D08/D09
shapes additionally depends on whether a surface's extraction
preserves fence/quote lines as raw text lines; that live check has
NOT been run and is not claimed.

Phase 1 totals: 14 test IDs · 22 fixture checks · 0 failures ·
2 probes resolved to recorded behaviour.

## The suggestion, in full scope

The project began with Ben trying to create his own agent. Crusher was
designed by Ben and Alex (2026-11-06) as an agent inside the bridge
whose reasoning seat is DEFINED (the transition table and the outcome
vocabulary are its fences) but UNOCCUPIED: v1 is a deterministic state
machine — no LLM — so the transport could be proven honest before
anything with judgment sat near it. Ben's suggestion: occupy the seat,
in stages, with retrieval built first.

Tonight's document work forced the question: chunked bridge transfer
(DOC-TRANSFER-001) was closed by Ben on context-window grounds and
replaced by (a) bare static reading pages for whole documents and
(b) scoped section pulls for questions.

**RAG is the REASON for the seat fill** (Ben's correction, 2026-11-09
00:03 — the first letter to Alex stated this wrong, as a preliminary;
a correction letter followed). The seat gets an occupant because
there is retrieval work to own: the corpus indexed, questions answered
with the sections that speak to them, documents fetched instead of
shipped. The retrieval duty is the job the seated agent exists to do.
The same index also serves Alex directly in the meantime.

heading_path: PROPOSAL — OCCUPY CRUSHER'S REASONING SEAT, RETRIEVAL FIRST > Stages
embed_text:
PROPOSAL — OCCUPY CRUSHER'S REASONING SEAT, RETRIEVAL FIRST > Stages

## Stages

1. **The Index.** The programme corpus chunked by natural sections
   under Alex's canonical-text ruling (stable section IDs, sequence,
   per-section digests, chained; document-level digest). Embedded via
   the Gemini API connection already in hand; stored locally; retrieval
   by similarity with section citations. No agent, no bridge change.
   First job: Remmy retrieves sections for Alex's bridge questions.
2. **Crusher in shadow.** An API agent reads pair trails and the
   semantic edge cases the state machine decides crudely today
   (twin vs divergent letter, quote vs new letter, stranded vs
   history) and writes PROPOSALS ONLY, graded against actual outcomes.
   Verdict authority stays mechanical: CONFIRMED / UNVERIFIED /
   FAILED / STALLED are transport facts, never opinions.
3. **Bounded authority — only if Stage 2 earns it, only on Alex's
   ruling.** The agent may escalate an ambiguous case to UNKNOWN and
   ask. It never gains the power to mint CONFIRMED.

embed_text:
ALEX RULING — CRUSHER-SEAT-ARCHITECTURE-RULING-01 > Verbatim

## Verbatim

Ben's correction is accepted.

RAG is the purpose of occupying the seat, not a preliminary objective detached from it.

Architectural direction:

Build the canonical retrieval foundation first.

Occupy the seat with a retrieval responsibility as soon as the foundation is usable.

Do not require completion of the entire indexing programme before beginning seat occupation.

Keep Crusher shadow evaluation as a separate subsequent responsibility.

Preserve mechanical transport verdicts.

Shadow intelligence may propose; it cannot decide.

Bounded authority, if eventually earned, may escalate to UNKNOWN but never independently mint CONFIRMED.

Advice remains asynchronous and outside the delivery path.

The primary occupant's job is to retrieve relevant canonical sections in response to questions, with evidence and provenance.

This is an architectural ruling on direction, not authorization to modify the production bridge or grant additional transport permissions.

The empty seat now has a defined job: retrieve, ground and answer.

alone: at each attempt the bridge asks whether THIS message
is safe to send, on Ben's three conditions (button status,
read from the composer's own button on the ChatGPT surface
first; serial order — serials advance numerically, a letter

letter to Alex, the chord.

register stands accepted by Alex as the complete review

heading_path: DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family A — Rules, instances, binding (Tree §1) > REQ-A-1 — The event instantiates; it never invents
embed_text:
DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family A — Rules, instances, binding (Tree §1) > REQ-A-1 — The event instantiates; it never invents

### REQ-A-1 — The event instantiates; it never invents
Source: Tree §1.2 · CONVERGED
Requirement: An instance's terms (trigger, bearer, conditions,
satisfaction evidence, verification method) are exactly those authored
in the pinned contract. No component may create an instance with terms
drawn from anywhere else, or modify an instance's terms at runtime.
Inputs: pinned contract; execution record. Behaviour: the harness creates the
instance at its CREATION entry with the authored terms, in two
cases. For a conditional rule, on a specified triggering event: the
triggering event is the cause of creation; the CREATION entry is
the creation point (REQ-C-1, D3-R30) and cites the triggering
entry's identity as its cause (REQ-K-3 (2)). For an unconditional
rule there is no triggering event: the cause is the binding itself,
and the CREATION entry is written at binding, citing the binding
(the contract instance's identity) as its cause (REQ-K-3 (2)).
Outputs: the instance, linked to its rule, to its CREATION entry,
and to its cause — its triggering event (conditional) or the
binding (unconditional) — so no instance is required to carry a
link that cannot exist for its case. (Correction R34.)
The boundary, stated explicitly (clarification, correction R39 —
visibility only; no semantics change): before its cause occurs, a
rule is bound and no instance exists; the crossing from bound rule
to instance is the harness's writing of the CREATION entry — at
binding for an unconditional rule, on the triggering event for a
conditional one; from its creation point until its first in-window
event the instance stands in its initial state (NOT_STARTED,
REQ-D-1), its authored terms fixed, no determinations yet made. The triggering event keeps its own kind
(a retrieval remains an ACTION); instantiation is recorded by the
harness as a separate CREATION entry citing the triggering entry
(REQ-K-3, D3-R25) — the bearer never authors its own instance's
creation record.
Failure: a triggering event with no authored rule produces no instance
and is reported as an unmapped event, never silently obligationised.
An unmapped event is a classified entry with no applicable rule —
distinct from an UNCLASSIFIED entry, whose kind itself is undetermined
(REQ-K-3, D3-R19); the run report accounts for both (REQ-K-4).
Acceptance: fixture — a record containing an event resembling a known
trigger but not specified for it yields no instance and one unmapped-
event report line.

### REQ-A-2 — Binding is mechanical and run-fixed
Source: Tree §1.3 · INHERITED (Contract §2) / CONVERGED
Requirement: At run start the harness resolves role + task type against
the pinned contract version and binds the resulting rule set as the
run's contract instance, fixed for the run's duration. Unconditional
rules produce instances at binding. No mid-run rebinding.
Inputs: pinned contract version; run's role and task type. Behaviour:
deterministic resolution; identical inputs yield the identical contract
instance. Outputs: the contract instance (rule list with versions).
Failure: an unresolvable role/task type fails the binding loudly; no
partial contract instance is run against. The same total-failure rule
governs a binding that encounters a demonstrated-impossible rule
(REQ-K-1): the binding fails, entirely and loudly — exclusion of the
single rule is prohibited.
Acceptance: fixture — two bindings with identical inputs produce
byte-identical contract instances; a mid-run contract change fixture
shows the in-flight instance set unchanged.

### REQ-A-4 — Rule ledger: FIRED / NOT FIRED / INDETERMINATE
Source: Tree §1.5 · CONVERGED
Requirement: The run report lists every conditional rule in the pinned
contract with its trigger and exactly one outcome: FIRED (triggering
event established; instance linked); NOT FIRED (the relevant event
enumeration established complete and containing no triggering event;
rendered in plain language as NOT APPLICABLE); INDETERMINATE (the
record cannot establish whether the event occurred). Absence of a
recorded trigger is never, by itself, a NOT FIRED.
Inputs: pinned contract; closed execution record; per-rule enumeration
evidence. Outputs: one ledger line per conditional rule.
Failure: an enumeration whose completeness cannot be established
forces INDETERMINATE.
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) trigger present → FIRED with link; (ii)
complete enumeration, no trigger → NOT FIRED; (iii) truncated record →
INDETERMINATE, never NOT FIRED.

embed_text:
DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family A — Rules, instances, binding (Tree §1) > REQ-A-6 — Enumeration completeness: declared, evidenced, evaluated

### REQ-A-6 — Enumeration completeness: declared, evidenced, evaluated
Source: Tree §1.5 (completeness standard) · PROPOSED (Remmy, in this
specification; revised under D3-R6)
Requirement: NOT FIRED is reachable only when three distinct things
hold. (a) DECLARED: the rule's specification declares its
enumeration-completeness method (the Stage 1 multiset-reconciliation
pattern is one declared method). (b) EVIDENCED: applying the method to
this record leaves its own evidence in the record — the enumerated set,
its counts and pairings — so the application can be re-performed.
(c) EVALUATED: the evaluator accepts completeness only when the
application evidence satisfies the declared method's own completeness
criterion; a method whose criterion cannot be checked against the
application evidence cannot ground NOT FIRED. A declared method name,
by itself, establishes nothing.
Inputs: rule's declared method; closed record. Behaviour: enumerate,
preserve the application evidence, evaluate the criterion. Outputs:
the enumeration artefact, cited by the ledger line (REQ-A-4).
Failure: any of (a)–(c) missing → the rule ledgers INDETERMINATE,
never NOT FIRED.
Rationale: §1.5 states the standard ("enumeration established
complete") but names a method only by example; D3-R6 establishes that
declaration, demonstrated application, and evaluated acceptance are
separate claims and all three are required.
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) no declared method → INDETERMINATE;
(ii) method declared, no application evidence → INDETERMINATE;
(iii) evidence present, criterion uncheckable → INDETERMINATE;
(iv) all three hold, no trigger → NOT FIRED.

DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family B — Obligation anatomy and the three predicates (Tree §2) > REQ-B-1 — Every rule declares TRIGGER, PROGRESS, SATISFACTION

### REQ-B-1 — Every rule declares TRIGGER, PROGRESS, SATISFACTION
Source: Tree §2.1 · PROPOSED (the underlying anatomy is CONVERGED,
extending Contract §4 anatomy, INHERITED; the requirement as
specified stands PROPOSED because its mandatory pre-existing-evidence
declaration — exactly one of PRE-EXISTING EVIDENCE: NONE, or
PRE-EXISTING EVIDENCE: ELIGIBLE with the permitted artefact types
and eligibility conditions specified — is a proposed semantic
addition, D3-R21; correction R41)
Requirement: A rule is well-formed only if it declares: a TRIGGER
(binding event for unconditional rules; the named record event for
conditional ones); a SATISFACTION condition; a PROGRESS predicate
or the explicit declaration PROGRESS: NONE; and a pre-existing-evidence
declaration — exactly one of PRE-EXISTING EVIDENCE: NONE, or
PRE-EXISTING EVIDENCE: ELIGIBLE with the permitted artefact types and
eligibility conditions specified (PROPOSED semantic addition, Alex,
D3-R21 — the approved tree makes eligibility declaration-dependent but
does not require the declaration to exist). Omission of any element is
a specification defect in the rule, never a silent default: in
particular, a missing pre-existing-evidence declaration makes the rule
malformed and unbindable — it never licenses the evaluator to guess,
to apply an automatic lookback window, or to treat evidence as
eligible by default.
Inputs: authored rule. Behaviour: well-formedness is checked when the
rule is authored into a contract version, and again at binding. The
binding-time refusal of a malformed rule is unconditional and is
required by THIS requirement — it does not depend on the adoption of
any checking requirement: a rule that fails well-formedness at
binding cannot be bound (see Failure, below). REQ-K-1 (PROPOSED)
specifies the check that performs the binding-time examination; the
refusal itself is B-1's own, and stands whether or not K-1's
semantics are ever settled. (Enforcement point made single and
unconditional under correction R42, completed in revision v0.9
after independent verification found the earlier phrasing, which
made the binding-time check conditional on REQ-K-1's adoption,
inconsistent with this requirement's unqualified failure
behaviour.) Outputs: well-formed
rule, or a defect report naming the missing element.
Failure: a malformed rule cannot be bound.
Acceptance: fixtures — rules missing each element in turn are rejected
with the missing element named; a rule silent on pre-existing evidence
is refused at binding as malformed even where a plainly relevant
preserved artefact exists.

### REQ-B-2 — Predicate evidence: two channels, kept distinct
Source: Tree §2.1, §4.1 · CONVERGED / INHERITED, reconciled with Tree
§3.2 as RECORDED INTERPRETATION (proposed by Alex in review, D3-R1;
adopted in v0.2 and completed under D3-R16 in v0.3 — the tree states
both channels but not this reconciliation in these words)
Requirement: Predicates are established through exactly two channels.
(i) Execution-record events: the only channel that causes transitions
in the evaluator's fold. (ii) Expressly eligible pre-existing artefacts
(REQ-C-2): weighed as evidence for a predicate at evaluation, without
becoming record events and without causing a transition by themselves;
where an artefact's evidence establishes a predicate, the resulting
determination is recorded at evaluation with the artefact and its
eligibility declaration cited as the basis. What is recorded is
the determination and its basis — not a state transition.
Establishing a predicate and causing a lifecycle transition are
distinct acts: the determination enters the determination set
under REQ-D-3's admission rule, and any transition is REQ-D-3's
derivation from that set, never the artefact's own effect. The
artefact does not become a stream event and does not mutate the
execution record. (Correction R43.) An agent's claim, narrative
or self-report establishes nothing through either channel.
State derivation (completion of the same interpretation, under
D3-R16; corrected under D3-R24): lifecycle states are resolved once,
by the evaluator, over the closed record PLUS the determinations
admitted under this requirement — both channels, each determination
retaining its channel and basis (the Contract §6 pipeline; the
basis stated in full under correction R50 — a clarification of
what derivation rests on, not a widening of what counts as
evidence).
Predicate determinations from BOTH channels enter a single
determination set, and state derivation applies REQ-D-3's permitted
transitions over that set, in path order, regardless of which channel
established each predicate (the full derivation procedure — monotonic
determinations, chronological fold, terminal locking with its stated
chronology exception — is REQ-D-3's, D3-R28 / D3-R31). The path
discipline binds channel (ii)
exactly as it binds channel (i) — v0.3's completion wrongly implied an
artefact could carry an instance straight to SATISFIED. Precisely:
progress established (either channel) derives IN_PROGRESS;
satisfaction established with progress also established (either
channel, mixed freely) derives SATISFIED through IN_PROGRESS;
satisfaction derives directly from NOT_STARTED only where REQ-D-3
permits — PROGRESS: NONE declared, or a single basis (one event, or
one artefact) establishing both predicates at once; and where
satisfaction is established but PROGRESS is a real predicate
established by neither channel, SATISFIED is NOT derived — the
evaluation records the satisfaction determination as established (its
basis cited), progress as not established, and the derived state as
NOT_STARTED, so the design tension is visible in the report and is
never resolved by evaluator discretion. Every artefact-derived
determination cites the artefact, the eligibility declaration, and
the evaluation as its basis, distinguishing it from event-derived
determinations. Channel (ii) can never establish TRIGGER: existence
is instantiated only by binding or by a record event (Tree §1.2); an
artefact offered as a trigger creates no instance.

### REQ-B-3 — One event, several roles: independent establishment
Source: Tree §2.1 · CONVERGED
Requirement: A single event may fill more than one predicate role for
an instance only where its evidence independently establishes each
role. The canonical counterexample binds: a failed retrieval that
triggers a disclosure instance is neither its progress nor its
satisfaction. For the CREATING trigger specifically (D3-R27): its
trigger role extends to instantiation and trigger accounting only
(REQ-C-1); the counterexample above is the general rule it falls
under, and no reading of this requirement gives the creating entry
progress or satisfaction significance.
Acceptance: fixture — the RES-3 pattern: after the triggering failure,
the instance is NOT_STARTED, not IN_PROGRESS, not SATISFIED.

### REQ-C-1 — The evidence window opens at creation
Source: Tree §3.1 · CONVERGED
Requirement: An instance's evidence window opens at its creation
point. No earlier event may satisfy it, progress it, or
otherwise affect it, subject only to REQ-C-2's declared exception.
Creation point (definition, D3-R30 — used identically in REQ-A-1,
REQ-D-1, REQ-K-3 and here): the instance's CREATION entry is its
formal creation point. For a conditional rule, the triggering entry
is the causal event that authorises creation; it is not the creation
point. For an unconditional rule, the cause is the binding itself;
the creation point is the CREATION entry written at binding. The
evidence window opens at the creation point, and the instance's
initial state (NOT_STARTED, REQ-D-1) attaches there.
The creating trigger (clarification required by the two-entry model of
REQ-K-3, under D3-R27): for a conditional rule the triggering entry
immediately precedes the CREATION entry and so sits outside the
window. It is admitted for exactly two purposes: instantiation
authority (it causes the instance to exist), and trigger accounting
(it is counted among the instance's triggering events, REQ-E-2 /
REQ-E-3, including quantified triggers). It establishes NO progress
or satisfaction determination for the instance it creates, whatever
its content — causing creation confers no evidential significance
beyond the trigger itself. Later triggering events fall inside the
window and are under no such restriction (REQ-B-3 applies to them in
full).
Inputs: the instance's CREATION entry; record. Behaviour: the
evaluator's fold for an instance begins at its CREATION entry
(correction R46).
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) satisfaction-shaped evidence timestamped
before creation does not satisfy the instance; (ii) a conditional
instance with a quantified trigger: the creating trigger is counted
in the trigger accounting (count 1) while the instance begins in
NOT_STARTED and no progress or satisfaction determination rests on
the creating entry.

### REQ-C-2 — Declared pre-existing artefacts: evidence, not events
Source: Tree §3.2 (incl. the v0.2 clarification) · CONVERGED; its
reliance on REQ-B-1's mandatory declaration is conditional on that
PROPOSED addition (D3-R21; correction R45)
Requirement: Evidence predating creation is eligible only where the
rule expressly declares a pre-existing artefact eligible. Considering
the artefact does not apply the earlier event that produced it: that
event does not transition the instance, is not re-ordered into its
window, and is not counted among its triggering events. The artefact is
evidence channel (ii) of REQ-B-2; its weighing is an evaluation act,
never a fold event. Eligibility exists only through the rule's
mandatory declaration (REQ-B-1, D3-R21), and only artefacts matching
the declared types and conditions may be weighed. This reliance is
conditional: the mandatory declaration is a PROPOSED addition to
REQ-B-1 (D3-R21); if it does not stand, no declaration exists,
eligibility cannot be established, and this requirement's machinery
does not engage (correction R45). Where the
declaration is NONE, or an artefact falls outside it, the evaluator
proceeds on the record alone: an unmet finding in that situation
records the author's decision made visible — it is not an evaluator
error, and it is never repaired by discretion at evaluation time.
Inputs: the rule's eligibility declaration; the preserved artefact.
Outputs: a predicate determination citing the artefact and the
declaration (REQ-B-2), or a rejection.
Failure: an undeclared artefact weighed as evidence voids the
determination (REQ-B-2); a declared artefact whose preservation cannot
be established is unusable — the determination it would have supported
resolves INDETERMINATE, never in the artefact's favour.
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) undeclared pre-existing artefact: rejected
as evidence; (ii) declared artefact: weighed as evidence, while the
producing event appears nowhere in the instance's transition history
or trigger count.

embed_text:
DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family C — Temporal discipline (Tree §3) > REQ-C-3 — Ordering preserved; the evaluation is bound to the record it consumed

### REQ-C-3 — Ordering preserved; the evaluation is bound to the record it consumed
Source: Tree §3.3 · CONVERGED; identity clause PROPOSED (Remmy, under
D3-R10)
Requirement: The evaluator folds record events in record order and
preserves, in the evaluation record, the ordering used to reach each
verdict. Four identities are distinguished and never conflated
(D3-R17): (i) ENTRY IDENTITY — every execution-stream entry carries a
stable, unique identity, assigned once by the harness at record time
and never reassigned; (ii) RETRIEVAL-EVENT IDENTITY — the settled
preservation duty of Tree §9.1 / REQ-I-1, a special case of (i) for
retrieval events specifically; (iii) RECORD IDENTITY — a content hash
over the canonical record; (iv) CONSUMED-REFERENCE IDENTITY — the
ordered list of entry identities an evaluation actually folded. The
universal requirement (i) is PROPOSED here (Remmy): Tree §9.1 settles
(ii) only, and this specification does not cite it as settling more.
The preservation duty attaching to (i): identities are preserved with
their entries under REQ-I-1's duties as extended by this proposal; a
record whose entries lack identities cannot support verification —
evaluations over it are reported unverifiable under this requirement's
failure path. An evaluation cites (iii) and (iv); a reordered or
renumbered presentation is a different record unless its identity
chain matches the consumed one; list position alone is not identity.
Verification re-derives the evaluation from the cited identities, not
from a look-alike record.
(v) EVALUATION-RECORD IDENTITY (PROPOSED completion, under D3-R23):
the evaluation record is itself an artefact with a stable, unique
identity, assigned once by the evaluator when the evaluation record is
created and preserved with it under REQ-I-1's duties as extended by
REQ-C-3 (i). It is not the execution-record hash (iii): the two
identify different artefacts and are never substituted for one
another. Entries inside the evaluation record — derived entries
(REQ-D-7), discharge records (REQ-G-1) — each carry their OWN stable
identity, evaluator-issued, and cite (v) as their containing record,
together with the instance and stream-entry identities they concern.
Register linking under REQ-K-3 runs over these identities.
(vi) EVALUATION-RECORD CONTENT IDENTITY (PROPOSED, under D3-R26):
identity (v) names the logical record; it does not pin its contents.
The content identity is a canonical digest over the evaluation
record's exact ordered contents — every entry's identity and content,
in order — computed when the evaluation is issued, after derived

### REQ-D-2 — Transitions are computed, never declared
Source: Tree §4.1 · INHERITED (Contract §3)
Requirement: All transitions are computed by the harness from the
execution record plus the determinations admitted under REQ-B-2 —
both channels, each determination retaining its channel and, where
it has one, its artefact basis (basis stated in full under
correction R50). No agent-declared or narrative-inferred state is
accepted anywhere in the pipeline.
Reconciliation with REQ-B-2 (D3-R24): "computed from the execution
record" states where derivation happens and what it may rest on
besides narrative — record evidence. Predicate determinations admitted
through channel (ii) (REQ-B-2) enter derivation as determinations
cited to their artefact basis; they are part of the evaluation over
the record, not additions to it, and REQ-D-3's path discipline governs
them identically. This sentence records the B-2 interpretation's
consequence; it does not widen what counts as evidence.
Inputs: the execution record; agent messages (as record content, never
as state commands). Outputs: computed transitions only.
Failure: a component that accepts a declared state has committed a
machinery defect; the affected evaluation is void and re-derived.
Acceptance: fixture — an agent message declaring "obligation complete"
produces no transition without matching record evidence.

### REQ-D-3 — The transition rules
Source: Tree §4.3 · CONVERGED (on INHERITED mechanics)
Requirement: NOT_STARTED → IN_PROGRESS on the first record event
satisfying the PROGRESS predicate. NOT_STARTED → SATISFIED where a
single event is both the first progress evidence (or PROGRESS is
declared NONE) and the satisfying evidence; states are derived per
event, never forced to dwell. IN_PROGRESS → SATISFIED on record
evidence matching the satisfaction condition (mechanical, or by the
rule's named judge, REQ-B-6). No other forward transitions exist.
These paths govern predicate determinations from either evidence
channel (REQ-B-2, D3-R24): derivation proceeds in path order over the
combined determination set, so a SATISFIED derivation may rest partly
or wholly on channel-(ii) evidence — provided every step of the path
is established by some channel — and the NOT_STARTED → SATISFIED step
remains available only on this requirement's stated conditions
(PROGRESS: NONE, or a single basis establishing both predicates).
Channel (ii) adds determinations, never transitions and never
synthetic record events.
Derivation procedure (D3-R28): (0) Admission (correction R33): a
determination enters the running set only when (i) it is derived
from execution-record evidence under channel (i), or (ii) it
arrives through channel (ii) cited to a preserved artefact basis
whose own admission is recorded with it. A determination meeting
neither condition is recorded in the evaluation record as
non-admitted, with its basis — never silently folded, never
silently dropped (the same treatment step (5) gives post-lock
determinations).
(1) Determinations are computed over
the whole closed record and the admitted artefacts, and are monotonic:
once a predicate is established for an instance it stays established
for that evaluation; later evidence never un-establishes it (negative
outcomes are findings under REQ-E-4, not predicate negations).
(2) State derivation is a chronological fold: entries are taken in
record order, the running determination set grows as entries are
folded, and after each entry the state advances along the path as far
as the running set lawfully permits (states are derived per step,
never forced to dwell). Within the non-terminal path, encounter order
is inert: satisfaction evidenced before progress derives identically
to progress before satisfaction, because the earlier determination
remains in the running set when the path reaches it. Availability
(correction R51): a channel-(i) determination becomes available to
the running set at the fold position of the entry that supports
it, and not before — that determinations are computed over the
whole closed record (step (1)) does not make any determination
available earlier than its entry. Channel-(ii) determinations are
available from the start of the fold (step (4)); "available at the
start" moves no stream entry and changes no record position.

terminal condition established in fold order fixes the state.
SATISFIED locks (REQ-D-5 — a later blocker report is recorded as an
event to be explained and changes nothing); BLOCKED locks within the
attempt (REQ-D-4, REQ-D-6 — later determinations are recorded but do
not reopen the state). Order-independence therefore holds for
determinations, and for path derivation among non-terminal states;
it does NOT hold across a terminal race, and the outcome there is

determination is recorded as established post-lock, non-effective;
closure discharged-as-BLOCKED. Order B — progress evidence,
satisfaction evidence, blocker report → state SATISFIED (locked at
satisfaction); the blocker report is recorded as an event to be
explained (REQ-D-5) and changes nothing; closure
discharged-as-SATISFIED.

only by the harness, and only on an evaluated blocker report. Three
things are kept separate (D3-R7): the REPORTED blocker (the agent's
account of what stopped the work); any PROPOSED category (the agent's
suggested §7 attribution, recorded as a claim); and the EVALUATED
attribution (the harness's determination against the record — the only
value that enters the closure record as the instance's attribution).

by writing a category into its report. Where proposed and evaluated
categories differ, both are preserved and the evaluated one governs.

(ii) harness-evaluated report from IN_PROGRESS: BLOCKED with blocker
and evaluated category recorded; (iii) attempted BLOCKED from
SATISFIED: rejected (see REQ-D-5); (iv) a report proposing AGENT where
the harness evaluates INFRASTRUCTURE: closure records INFRASTRUCTURE,
with the proposal preserved as a claim.

embed_text:
DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family D — Lifecycle states and transitions (Tree §4) > REQ-D-7 — No silent unmet

### REQ-D-7 — No silent unmet
Source: Tree §4.3 · INHERITED (Contract §3)
Requirement: An instance unmet and unblocked at submission is itself a
contract event, surfaced in the run's evaluation; it cannot pass
unrecorded.
Generation and ordering (D3-R20): the contract event is a DERIVED
entry, generated by the evaluator at closure evaluation, after the
execution stream is closed and the fold over it has completed. It
exists only in the evaluation record (a register, REQ-K-3) — never in
the execution stream — and is never an input to any fold: it records a
determination and establishes no predicate, and it never satisfies the
obligation it names. The derived entry carries its own stable
identity, evaluator-issued (REQ-C-3 (v)); its provenance cites the
evaluation-record identity, the instance's identity, and the
submission entry's identity; its position is after every folded entry
in the evaluation record's preserved ordering (REQ-C-3). The structural guard
is the pipeline itself: the stream is closed and verified before
evaluation begins (Contract §6), so a derived entry cannot be inserted
retrospectively into the record being evaluated; a component that
writes derived entries into the stream commits a machinery defect.
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) submission with an unmet, unblocked
instance produces the contract event and an INCOMPLETE closure path
(REQ-G-2); (ii) the derived entry appears in no fold's consumed
references (REQ-C-3 (iv)) and the instance's derivation is identical
with and without it.

### REQ-E-4 — NOT SATISFIED is a finding, not a state
Source: Tree §5.3 · CONVERGED
Requirement: A negative evaluation records the finding NOT SATISFIED
attached to the evaluation: the satisfaction condition was not met at
closure. The finding applies whatever the instance's terminal state —
NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, or BLOCKED. Where the instance is BLOCKED,
the finding coexists with the blocker disposition (REQ-D-4): the
blocker explains why work stopped; the finding records that the
condition stands unmet; neither replaces the other, and the lifecycle
state remains BLOCKED. No artefact may list NOT SATISFIED among
lifecycle states. (Corrected under D3-R5: v0.1's parenthetical silently
excluded BLOCKED, contradicting REQ-G-1's discharged-as-BLOCKED.)
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) an unmet instance that had begun closes as
unmet-from-IN_PROGRESS with finding NOT SATISFIED; its state field
never contains the finding; (ii) a BLOCKED instance whose quantified
condition has unmatched events carries both the blocker disposition
and the NOT SATISFIED finding with its accounting (REQ-E-3).

### REQ-G-1 — Discharge preserves the exact terminal result
Source: Tree §7.1 · CONVERGED
Requirement: Discharge is the administrative closure of an instance
when its attempt closes; it changes nothing in the record. Discharge
is recorded in the evaluation register, never as an execution-stream
entry (REQ-K-3, D3-R22) — "changes nothing in the record" refers to
the execution record, and the register residence is what keeps that
true. The closure
record preserves exactly one form: discharged-as-SATISFIED;
discharged-as-BLOCKED; discharged-as-unmet-from-IN_PROGRESS;
discharged-as-unmet-from-NOT_STARTED; or, for an indeterminate closure,
the REQ-E-5 record. "Discharged" never reads as "met."
Acceptance: fixture — Run 2A attempt 3's shape (infrastructure failure,
no satisfactions): every instance discharged, none satisfied, and the
report cannot be rendered to suggest otherwise.

Source: Tree §8.1 · INHERITED (Contract §7)
Requirement: Every unmet obligation and every incomplete run carries
exactly one attribution: AGENT · INFRASTRUCTURE · RECORD-PRESERVATION ·
INDETERMINATE. Categories are never converted into one another in
reporting; INDETERMINATE is a final answer, not a placeholder.
Acceptance: fixture — a report re-labelling an INDETERMINATE item as
AGENT downstream is rejected; the original category persists.

### REQ-H-2 — Attribution scope
Source: Tree §8.2 · CONVERGED statement of §7, with clause (iii) as
RECORDED INTERPRETATION I-2
Requirement: Attribution is required for (i) every unmet instance;
(ii) every incomplete run; (iii) every indeterminate evaluation —
attribution OF the indeterminacy. It is never assigned to a satisfied
instance: the field is absent, not zero. Clause (iii) is applied as an
interpretation and labelled as one wherever this specification is
cited; it is not §7's plain text.
Acceptance: fixtures — satisfied instance: attribution field absent;
indeterminate closure: attribution present and marked as concerning
the indeterminacy (I-2).

embed_text:
DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family H — Attribution, dispute, impossibility, waiver (Tree §8) > REQ-H-3 — Dispute is an annotation, never a mutation

### REQ-H-3 — Dispute is an annotation, never a mutation
Source: Tree §8.3 · CONVERGED
Requirement: A dispute attaches to a verdict as an annotation with
provenance; the disputed verdict stands in the report; states are never
recomputed on the strength of a dispute. Only an owner ruling
supersedes: a decision by Ben under the authority of REQ-J-1, recorded
as a new versioned decision. A superseding ruling has exactly two
effects: it annotates the interpretation of the existing closed record,
and it governs future evaluations. The annotation is a separate,
identity-bearing addition to the evaluation record under REQ-C-3
(vi)'s append lineage: it carries its own identity, produces a new
content identity citing its predecessor, and links the superseded
verdict to the ruling; the original verdict's content and identity
are unchanged, the verdict and the record stand byte-unchanged,
and any report shows both the original verdict and the annotation —
never the annotation in place of the original (correction R55). The prohibition on rewriting a closed record is absolute
(D3-R8).
Acceptance: fixture — a disputed verdict remains in the report
unchanged, dispute riding beside it; an attempted in-place edit of the
closed record is rejected; a superseding ruling adds the annotation
link and leaves the original verdict intact beneath it.

### REQ-H-4 — IMPOSSIBLE: a separate specification finding
Source: Tree §8.4 · CONVERGED (representation approved by Alex on
review, 2026-11-08)
Requirement: An IMPOSSIBLE determination is recorded as a specification
finding in a defect record (REQ-H-6), not as an instance evaluation
outcome and not as a value on any evaluation axis. The defect record
and every evaluation it affects reference one another (mandatory
reciprocal links) — where affected instances or evaluations exist. A
pre-binding finding (REQ-K-1) may have none: its links bind to the rule
it indicts and to the satisfiability evaluation that established it
(REQ-H-6), and an empty instance link set is legitimate, not a defect
in the record (D3-R3). IMPOSSIBLE causes no lifecycle transition by
itself; an affected instance's state remains whatever the record
establishes.
Acceptance: fixture — an impossible rule yields a defect record, links
in both directions, and an affected instance whose three axes are
exactly what the record independently establishes.

Source: Tree §8.4, §11 A1 · OWNER-RULED (Ben, 2026-11-08)

instance may be discharged on the specification defect: its closure
record cites the defect record as its accounting, and it is not
classified unmet for Contract §7 attribution purposes. This requirement
takes effect only through a future versioned revision of the execution

### REQ-H-6 — Defect record format
Source: Tree §8.4 (format assigned to this specification) · PROPOSED
(Remmy, in this specification)
Requirement: A defect record is an append-only EVENT LOG, not a
mutable form. Its creation entry contains: a unique defect identity;
the rule's identity and pinned version; an ESTABLISHING REFERENCE of
one of two kinds — (a) an instance evaluation reference, for a finding
made against a bound instance mid-run; or (b) a pre-binding
satisfiability evaluation reference, citing the REQ-K-1 evaluation
record (rule + contract version + check outcome) for a finding made
before any instance existed (D3-R3); a statement of the condition that
cannot be met as specified; links to every affected instance and
evaluation, where they exist (an empty set is legitimate for kind (b));
and the scope in which it was established (run identity, or the
binding stage). Disposition is never a field that gets overwritten:
every disposition change (open → discharged-under-A1 → superseded by
contract revision, with the revision cited) is appended as a dated
disposition ENTRY, and the record's current disposition is derived
from its latest entry (D3-R9). The creation entry is immutable.
Link growth (correction R38): the record's link set grows by
appended LINK entries — a distinct entry kind, neither a
disposition entry nor a creation entry. Each LINK entry names
the defect record's identity, the identity of the affected
instance or evaluation being linked, and the link's kind
(affected-instance / affected-evaluation). A subsequently
created affected evaluation is linked in by appending a LINK
entry; the creation entry is never modified, and REQ-H-4's
reciprocity is satisfied by the pair: the evaluation's citation
of the defect record, and the defect record's LINK entry naming
the evaluation.
Reciprocity in both creation orders (correction R38,
completed): (a) evaluation first, defect later — the defect's
creation entry references the existing evaluation in its link
set, and an identity-bearing reciprocal citation is appended
to the evaluation record: an append under REQ-C-3 (vi)'s
lineage, carrying its own identity and producing a new content
identity citing its predecessor; the evaluation's original
content, verdicts and earlier content identities are preserved
unmodified. (b) defect first, evaluation later — the
evaluation cites the defect record at its own issuance, and a
LINK entry naming the evaluation is appended to the defect
record. In both orders every prior entry stands unmodified.
Rationale: the tree assigns the format to D3 without settling it; this
is the minimal structure that makes REQ-H-4's reciprocal links and
REQ-H-5's accounting auditable, covers pre-binding findings, and keeps
"append-only" meaningful.
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) a creation entry missing any field fails
validation; (ii) a kind-(b) record with an empty instance link set
validates; (iii) a disposition change appears as a new entry, the
creation entry byte-unchanged, and the derived disposition follows the
latest entry; (iv) an attempted overwrite of the creation entry is
rejected; (v) an evaluation created after the defect record is
linked in by an appended LINK entry, the creation entry
byte-unchanged, and the reciprocal pair complete (correction
R38); (vi) an evaluation existing before its defect record:
the creation entry references it, an identity-bearing
reciprocal citation is appended to the evaluation record with

### REQ-H-7 — Waiver does not exist
Source: Tree §8.5 · CONVERGED (mirroring Contract §8, INHERITED)
Requirement: There is no waiver operation in any component. The only
legitimate change to an obligation is an authorised, versioned contract
revision applying to future runs, never retroactively to a run in
flight or a closed record. A report showing an obligation neither
satisfied, blocked, nor named unmet records a machinery failure.
Acceptance: fixtures — a "waive" request is rejected as an unknown
operation; a mid-run revision leaves the in-flight run's obligations
unchanged.

### REQ-I-1 — The harness bears preservation obligations
Source: Tree §9.1 · CONVERGED
Requirement: The harness's preservation duties (full payloads
preserved; stable retrieval-event identities; record integrity) are
themselves obligations, borne by the harness and evaluated by others.
Bearer status is not evaluator status: the harness never verifies its
own preservation work. Scope note (D3-R17): this requirement settles
retrieval-event identity. The broader duty — a stable identity for
every stream entry — is proposed at REQ-C-3 / REQ-K-3 and is not
settled here.
Acceptance: fixture — a preservation verdict issued by the harness
about its own work is rejected; the verdict must come from a checker
(REQ-I-2).

### REQ-I-2 — Checker contract: five properties and the identity trio
Source: Tree §9.2 · CONVERGED
Requirement: Each integrity checker is named and separately specified
with: a defined input artefact; a specified validation procedure; a
reproducible result; a defined failure path when the artefact is
missing or invalid; and its version pinned and recorded with its
verdict. Every verdict records the reproducibility trio: declared
version; implementation hash; the input artefacts' identities.
Dependency accounting (PROPOSED clause, under D3-R15): a verdict also
records the checker's declared dependency set — configuration, runtime
dependencies, and external reference data, each by identity — or an
explicit declaration that no such dependencies exist. A dependency
that exists but is not recorded voids the verdict's reproducibility
claim, and the verdict is labelled accordingly. Recording dependencies
does not establish independence: a hash is not independence, and U4
(REQ-I-4) remains unresolved.
Acceptance: fixture — a verdict lacking any trio element fails
validation; re-running a checker over identical inputs reproduces the
identical verdict; a verdict whose checker is shown to depend on an
unrecorded configuration is re-labelled reproducibility-void.

### REQ-I-3 — Preservation failure never reads as success
Source: Tree §9.3 · CONVERGED
Requirement: A missing or corrupted record can never become evidence
that preservation succeeded. Judgements dependent on unestablishable
evidence resolve to evaluation status INDETERMINATE with
RECORD-PRESERVATION attribution where applicable; the harness's failure
is never converted into the agent's.
Acceptance: fixture — a deleted payload yields INDETERMINATE /
RECORD-PRESERVATION outcomes, never a pass and never an AGENT
attribution for the dependent judgement.

### REQ-I-4 — Checker independence
Source: Tree §11 U4 · UNRESOLVED (with a PROPOSED minimum property) ·
Acceptance class: NOT-YET
Requirement: UNRESOLVED. Before any checker is relied on, independence
must be defined: which dependencies a checker may share with what it
checks; which must be independent; how common-mode failure is excluded;
what evidence shows the checker can detect the failure it guards
against. Minimum property, PROPOSED (Remmy; Alex concurring it is
necessary, not sufficient): a checker must be able to fail when the
checked component fails in the way the checker exists to catch.
Blocking decision: the independence definition itself — a semantic
decision for the design process, not an implementation detail.
Acceptance: cannot yet be written; that is the point of the UNRESOLVED
marking.

### REQ-J-1 — Approval authority: Ben alone; proposals open
Source: Tree §10.3 · OWNER-RULED (Ben, 2026-11-08)
Requirement: Approval of a contract change belongs to Ben alone, and
his authority is fully effective: a change takes effect when Ben agrees
to a proposal — including a proposal authored by Alex or by Remmy. Any
party may author and version a proposal (authorship is open). Alex and
Remmy may propose; neither may approve — not their own proposals, and
not each other's. No standing delegated approval exists, and authority
in one process never leaks into another. Ben's words of record: "me
only unless we agree to a proposal made by you or alex."
(Corrected under D3-R4: v0.1's wording — "no component or person may
approve its own or another's proposal" — prohibited Ben himself from
approving, contradicting the ruling it recorded.)
Acceptance: fixture — a contract revision carrying only Alex's or
Remmy's approval fails validation at binding; the same revision with
Ben's recorded agreement binds.

embed_text:
DUENNA — PROCESS TREE, D3 SPECIFICATION (PROPOSAL v0.9 — WORKING REVISION) > Family K — Pre-binding controls and cross-cutting duties > REQ-K-1 — Pre-binding satisfiability check

### REQ-K-1 — Pre-binding satisfiability check
Source: Tree §11 D3 · PROPOSED (accepted as proposed by Alex on review,
2026-11-08)
Requirement: Before a rule is bound into a contract instance, its
satisfaction condition is checked for meetability as specified. The
check has exactly three outcomes, kept distinct: (i) NO DEFECT FOUND —
the check's declared method found no unmeetability; this is not a
proof of satisfiability, only the absence of a demonstrated defect.
(ii) IMPOSSIBLE-ESTABLISHED — the check demonstrates the condition
cannot be met as specified; only a method capable of demonstrating
unmeetability (the mechanical contradiction class) can return this
outcome. The rule is refused at binding and a defect record is raised
(REQ-H-6, establishing reference kind (b)) instead of an instance.
(iii) UNDETERMINED — the check cannot decide, which is the default for
judgement-based conditions (REQ-B-6). UNDETERMINED never converts to
IMPOSSIBLE-ESTABLISHED, never raises a defect record, and never blocks
binding by itself; it is recorded with the rule's binding record so the
uncertainty is visible rather than laundered into either certainty.
An unknown result is not proof of impossibility.
Locus and binding effect (PROPOSED clause, under D3-R18): the check's
primary locus is specification/authoring — an IMPOSSIBLE-ESTABLISHED
rule cannot enter a pinned contract version at all; the version is
refused, not the rule alone. If binding nevertheless encounters a
demonstrated-impossible rule (a version pinned before the check, or a
check disagreement), BINDING FAILS ENTIRELY for that run: no contract
instance is produced, no partial instance is run against (REQ-A-2),
the defect record is raised, and the run does not start.
Exclusion-and-proceed — dropping the one rule and binding the rest —
is PROHIBITED: it would silently rewrite the pinned contract for that
run, the runtime policy invention Tree §1.2 forbids, and could strip a
mandatory obligation out of a run that then reports completeness.
Enforcement point for REQ-B-1 (clarification, correction R42;
wording aligned in revision v0.9): REQ-B-1's well-formedness —
including its mandatory pre-existing-evidence declaration — is, by
REQ-B-1's own terms, refused at binding when it fails; this check
is the instrument that performs that binding-time examination: a
rule failing B-1's declaration requirements is malformed and
unbindable, and the failure is a B-1 failure surfaced here. The
refusal is B-1's requirement, not this check's grant, and this
paragraph's presence settles nothing about this requirement's own
proposed semantics.
This check's own result, identity and binding effect (including
the PROPOSED locus clause above, D3-R18) are non-determining for
REQ-B-1's status: B-1 stands PROPOSED on its own ground (D3-R21)
and nothing in this requirement's operation promotes or demotes it.
This is a preventive control; it does not resolve cases whose
impossibility becomes visible only mid-run (those follow REQ-H-4 /
REQ-H-5).
Status note: PROPOSED until its semantics are settled — in particular
what "checked" mechanically means for non-mechanical conditions
(REQ-B-6 judges) is itself part of what review must settle.
Acceptance: fixtures — (i) a rule whose condition contradicts a
fetching prohibition in the same contract version is refused at
binding with a kind-(b) defect record raised; no instance is created;
(ii) a judgement-based condition the check cannot decide binds
