### REQ-K-3 — Record taxonomy: kinds, roles, and the stream boundary
Source: presupposed by Tree §§1–5, nowhere enumerated · PROPOSED
(Remmy, in this specification; revised under D3-R2 and D3-R11)
Requirement: Three distinctions govern the record.
(1) KIND vs ROLE. Every entry in the execution-event stream has
exactly one KIND — what sort of entry it is. Predicate ROLES (trigger,
progress, satisfaction, per REQ-B-1) are not kinds: they are
assignments the evaluator computes per instance over entries, and one
entry may carry several roles, or none (REQ-B-3). No entry is ever
required to classify under a role name.
(2) STREAM KINDS (minimal proposed set): CREATION (the harness's
instantiation entries — one per instance created; the CREATION entry
is the instance's formal creation point, REQ-C-1 / D3-R30. For a conditional
rule, the CREATION entry is a separate entry from the triggering
entry: it carries its own identity (REQ-C-3 (i)), occupies the stream
position immediately following the triggering entry, and cites the
triggering entry's identity as its cause; where one event triggers
several instances, their CREATION entries form one contiguous
block immediately following the triggering entry: the first
follows the triggering entry, each subsequent entry follows the
preceding CREATION entry, in pinned-contract rule order, and no
unrelated stream entry may intervene in the block (correction
R37). For an unconditional rule, the CREATION
entry is written at binding and cites the binding (the contract
instance's identity) as its cause. A CREATION entry establishes no
predicate roles — trigger is a role the evaluator assigns to the
triggering entry (REQ-B-3), never to the CREATION entry. (D3-R25.));
ACTION (an attempt at work — a retrieval,
a fetch, a production, a communication); SUBMISSION; BLOCKER-REPORT;
CLOSURE (exactly one entry kind: the harness's record-sealing entry
that closes the stream — one per run, final position; administrative
discharge (REQ-G-1) and evaluator-derived closure findings (REQ-D-7)
are NOT stream entries and are never classified CLOSURE — they live in
the evaluation register, per (3) below and D3-R22); UNCLASSIFIED
(an entry the harness cannot determine the kind of — the honest sink:
it preserves the exactly-one-kind property and establishes no
predicate). UNCLASSIFIED is not UNMAPPED (D3-R19): an UNMAPPED EVENT
is a finding about a perfectly classifiable entry — kind known — for
which no authored rule applies (REQ-A-1); it is reported in the run
report (REQ-K-4), not forced into the taxonomy as a kind.
(3) THE BOUNDARY. Outside the stream, in linked registers, never
folded as events: checker verdicts (REQ-I-2); defect records (REQ-H-6);
dispute annotations (REQ-H-3); owner rulings (REQ-J-1, REQ-H-3);
administrative discharge records (REQ-G-1); and
evaluation-derived entries, including the unmet-at-submission contract
event (REQ-D-7), which live in the evaluation record under REQ-D-7's
generation rules. Registers link to stream entries and instances by
identity (REQ-C-3); they are evidence about the run, not events in it.
Every stream entry carries its stable identity (REQ-C-3 (i),
PROPOSED), its position in the record order (REQ-C-3) and the identity
of the instance(s) it concerns, or is explicitly instance-free.
Every CREATION entry identifies the instance it creates,
unconditional instances included — a CREATION entry is never
instance-free; for an unconditional instance the binding identity

### REQ-K-4 — Run report composition
Source: compiled from Tree §1.5, §5, §7, §9 · CONVERGED (as a
compilation of the cited duties)
Requirement: A run's report contains: the rule ledger (REQ-A-4); every
instance's evaluation record — three axes (REQ-E-1), per-event
accounting where quantified (REQ-E-3), findings (REQ-E-4), closure form
(REQ-G-1), each cited by its evaluation-record identity and content
identity (REQ-C-3 (v), (vi)), the content identity cited with its
canonicalization procedure identifier (D3-CANON-1, REQ-C-3);
defect records and their links
(REQ-H-4, REQ-H-6); checker
verdicts with their reproducibility trios (REQ-I-2); and the run's
closure outcome with its attribution (REQ-G-2, REQ-H-1); every
UNCLASSIFIED entry by identity (REQ-K-3); and every unmapped event —
a classified entry with no applicable authored rule (REQ-A-1,
D3-R19). A report
missing a component is incomplete as a report, whatever the run's own
outcome. Checker verdicts are reported as REPORTED evidence: their
presence, and their reproducibility trio, confer no trust by
themselves, and every report carrying them carries the standing caveat
that checker independence is UNRESOLVED (REQ-I-4, UX-1). Where an
evaluation relies on a checker verdict for a preservation judgement,
the reliance is stated explicitly in the evaluation record — reliance
is visible, never silent (D3-R12).
Acceptance: fixture — a report generator run over a synthetic closed
record emits every component; removing any one fails report
validation.

## UNRESOLVED register (consolidated)

- **UX-1 (Tree U4) — Checker independence.** Carried at REQ-I-4. The
  definition (shared vs independent dependencies, common-mode failure,
  demonstrated detection) is a semantic decision outstanding. The
  minimum property is PROPOSED only.
- **UX-2 (Tree U2) — Obligation clocks.** Carried at REQ-K-2. No clock
  semantics exist in this specification; the decision whether any
  obligation needs one remains open.
- **UX-3 — NOT FIRED enumeration methods.** REQ-A-6 (revised) proposes
  the declared / evidenced / evaluated structure. Until that proposal
  is settled, rules without a declared method ledger conservatively
  (FIRED or INDETERMINATE only) — the conservative behaviour is
  specified; the anatomy addition is not settled.
- **UX-4 — Satisfiability-check semantics.** REQ-K-1 is PROPOSED; its
  three-outcome structure is specified, but what the check mechanically
  consists of for judgement-based conditions (REQ-B-6) is unsettled
  and blocks K-1's full testability.
- **UX-5 — Taxonomy finality.** REQ-K-3's kind set and stream boundary
  are PROPOSED (revised under D3-R2/R11, again under D3-R19/R20 —
  UNCLASSIFIED split from unmapped events; derived entries moved to
  the evaluation register — and again under D3-R22, discharge excluded
  from the stream and CLOSURE narrowed to the record-sealing entry).
  If review extends them, dependent fixtures
  change; the fold semantics (REQ-C-3, REQ-E-5) do not.

Claude's finding: REQ-K-1 states B-1 is "enforced at binding by this check," while REQ-B-1's own Behaviour made the binding check conditional ("REQ-K-1 if adopted"), and K-1 is PROPOSED.

Changes (v0.9 revision only; the matrix's guard held — K-1's proposed semantics are NOT settled, R18/UX-4 untouched, K-1 remains PROPOSED):

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R60 — REQ-I-2 checker contract
class CheckerContract:
    """REQ-I-2 checker contract, as a standalone object (v0.9 — in
    v1.2 the checker was a closure defined inside the fixture, so
    the contract's properties could not be exercised independently
    of the test that asserted them). The contract DEFINES: the input
    artefact it accepts, the validation procedure it runs, and its
    pinned version. A verdict is stamped with all three; any
    divergence between a run and the contract is detectable from
    the verdict itself."""
    def __init__(self, input_id, procedure, version, pinned=True):
        self.input_id = input_id
        self.procedure = procedure
        self.version = version
        self.pinned = pinned

    def run(self, artefact):
        if not self.pinned:
            return "REJECTED: unpinned version"
        if artefact is None:
            return "FAILURE-PATH: missing input artefact"
        if artefact.get("id") != self.input_id:
            return f"REJECTED: artefact is not the defined input ({self.input_id})"
        if artefact.get("corrupt"):
            return "FAILURE-PATH: invalid artefact"
        digest = hashlib.sha256(artefact["payload"].encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
        return {"verdict": f"preserved sha={digest}", "input": self.input_id,
                "procedure": self.procedure, "version": self.version}

def fixture_r60():
    contract = CheckerContract("ART-INPUT-1", "REQ-I-3 preservation check", "checker-v1.3")
    art = {"id": "ART-INPUT-1", "payload": "payload-1"}
    # (a) defined input artefact: the defined input runs; any other
    # artefact is refused — the input is a contract term, not a
    # parameter the caller may vary silently.
    run_defined = contract.run(art)
    check("FX-R60a", "R60", "REQ-I-2 defined input artefact: defined input accepted; a different artefact refused",
          ("verdict", "REJECTED: artefact is not the defined input (ART-INPUT-1)"),
          ("verdict" if isinstance(run_defined, dict) else run_defined,
           contract.run({"id": "ART-OTHER", "payload": "payload-1"})))
    # (b) validation procedure: the verdict carries the contract's
    # procedure; a verdict stamped with another procedure is not
    # this contract's output.
    v = contract.run(art)
    forged = {**v, "procedure": "some other procedure"}
    check("FX-R60b", "R60", "REQ-I-2 validation procedure: verdict stamped with the contract procedure; foreign procedure stamp detected",
          ("REQ-I-3 preservation check", True),
          (v["procedure"], forged["procedure"] != contract.procedure))
    # (c) reproducible result: two runs over the same input produce
    # byte-identical verdicts.
    check("FX-R60c", "R60", "REQ-I-2 reproducible result: repeated runs produce identical verdicts",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R60 — REQ-I-2 checker contract
class CheckerContract:
    """REQ-I-2 checker contract, as a standalone object (v0.9 — in
    v1.2 the checker was a closure defined inside the fixture, so
    the contract's properties could not be exercised independently
    of the test that asserted them). The contract DEFINES: the input
    artefact it accepts, the validation procedure it runs, and its
    pinned version. A verdict is stamped with all three; any
    divergence between a run and the contract is detectable from
    the verdict itself."""
    def __init__(self, input_id, procedure, version, pinned=True):
        self.input_id = input_id
        self.procedure = procedure
        self.version = version
        self.pinned = pinned

    def run(self, artefact):
        if not self.pinned:
            return "REJECTED: unpinned version"
        if artefact is None:
            return "FAILURE-PATH: missing input artefact"
        if artefact.get("id") != self.input_id:
            return f"REJECTED: artefact is not the defined input ({self.input_id})"
        if artefact.get("corrupt"):
            return "FAILURE-PATH: invalid artefact"
        digest = hashlib.sha256(artefact["payload"].encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
        return {"verdict": f"preserved sha={digest}", "input": self.input_id,
                "procedure": self.procedure, "version": self.version}

def fixture_r60():
    contract = CheckerContract("ART-INPUT-1", "REQ-I-3 preservation check", "checker-v1.3")
    art = {"id": "ART-INPUT-1", "payload": "payload-1"}
    # (a) defined input artefact: the defined input runs; any other
    # artefact is refused — the input is a contract term, not a
    # parameter the caller may vary silently.
    run_defined = contract.run(art)
    check("FX-R60a", "R60", "REQ-I-2 defined input artefact: defined input accepted; a different artefact refused",
          ("verdict", "REJECTED: artefact is not the defined input (ART-INPUT-1)"),
          ("verdict" if isinstance(run_defined, dict) else run_defined,
           contract.run({"id": "ART-OTHER", "payload": "payload-1"})))
    # (b) validation procedure: the verdict carries the contract's
    # procedure; a verdict stamped with another procedure is not
    # this contract's output.
    v = contract.run(art)
    forged = {**v, "procedure": "some other procedure"}
    check("FX-R60b", "R60", "REQ-I-2 validation procedure: verdict stamped with the contract procedure; foreign procedure stamp detected",
          ("REQ-I-3 preservation check", True),
          (v["procedure"], forged["procedure"] != contract.procedure))
    # (c) reproducible result: two runs over the same input produce
    # byte-identical verdicts.
    check("FX-R60c", "R60", "REQ-I-2 reproducible result: repeated runs produce identical verdicts",
          True, contract.run(art) == contract.run(dict(art)))
    # (d) failure path for missing / invalid artefacts.
    check("FX-R60d", "R60", "REQ-I-2 failure paths: missing artefact and invalid artefact both take the failure path, never a verdict",
          ("FAILURE-PATH: missing input artefact", "FAILURE-PATH: invalid artefact"),
          (contract.run(None), contract.run({"id": "ART-INPUT-1", "payload": "x", "corrupt": True})))

D3 v0.9 — FIXTURE RESULTS (revision build) > What changed for the six findings

## What changed for the six findings

- **R47** — FX-R47b now runs a conditional trigger whose content WOULD qualify
  (PROGRESS + SATISFACTION predicates carried on the trigger entry) and shows
  the fold establishing nothing from it, with a control run proving the same
  predicates satisfy when supplied as admitted determinations. FX-R47c's
  INDETERMINATE is now emitted by the fold's own REQ-C-2 resolution, not
  written by the test.
- **R56** — split into FX-R56a (the full three-way separation holds; each
  role's verdict independently necessary, exercised by removing each role in
  turn) and FX-R56b (every prohibited substitution: evaluator->examiner,
  examiner->gate, evaluator->gate, plus self-verification — each rejected).
- **R60** — the checker is now a standalone CheckerContract object defined by
  the harness, not a closure inside the fixture. FX-R60a–e exercise the five
  properties independently: defined input artefact, validation procedure,
  reproducible result, failure paths, pinned/recorded version.
- **R63** — FX-R63a validates the creation block against a stream the binding
  machinery actually produced, with an interleaved stream as a negative case.
  FX-R63c (new) exercises the matrix's third item: every entry's stable
  identity, record position, and instance identity or declared instance-free
  status, with tampered-position and missing-identity negatives. FX-R63b also
  covers the valid role-free entry.
- **R65** — FX-R65 now mismatches each of the five provenance relationships in
  turn (evaluation_record, content_identity, procedure, defect_link,
  verdict_trio); each fails validation while every component is present.

## Discrepancies against the implementer's reconciliation

Each is named individually and left unresolved for adjudication.

1. **D1, approval state (three-way).** The handoff says "APPROVED WITH STATED CONDITIONS by Alex". The reconciliation says "D3 approval: NOT given". The v0.8 header says "NOT APPROVED".
2. **D2, approval authority.** The handoff says Alex holds delegated approval authority from Ben. REQ-J-1 says approval "belongs to Ben alone… No standing delegated approval exists." The spec header says approval is "Alex's".
3. **D3, R59.** The reconciliation says "the R60/R61 renumbering". The matrix says the REQ-I-3 finding was numbered R59 and renumbered R61. R60 is a different finding.
4. **D4, R42.** The reconciliation says "Implemented (Stage 2)". REQ-B-1 was never amended, so the correction is only partly carried.
5. **D5, coverage overstated for R47, R56, R63, R65.** The reconciliation reports these as implemented, executed, and passed. The matrix's named items are not all exercised.
6. **D6, R60.** The reconciliation says all five properties are tested. Two are not separately exercised.
7. **D7, v0.7 identity.** The reconciliation says the file is `a14cad05…` with canonical hash `28718d26…`. The register gives `28718d26…` as the file's own SHA-256. The results document also cites `a14cad05…`. The v0.7 file is not in the package, so this is NOT VERIFIED.
8. **D8, harness identity in the results document.** It cites harness v1.1, SHA `20a6767f…`, 27,971 bytes. The delivered harness is `89dc0e50…`, 28,324 bytes, self-labelled v1.2, as the reconciliation and JSON say.
9. **D9, results.json identity.** The results document cites SHA `fd3378ef…`. The delivered file hashes to `4df5c0ba…`. The size, 8,881 bytes, does match.
10. **D10, R34 erratum.** The reconciliation cites a "matrix-row erratum" in the change record. No such erratum appears in the matrix, and the change record is not in the package. NOT VERIFIED.
11. **D11, R48 provenance.** The spec cites "Alex's rework direction, pb-mwa9mpq7". The matrix row does not mention it, and neither the reconciliation nor the package shows the rework approval. NOT VERIFIED.

Agreements: R33–R58 text placement, the 15 / 2 / 14 kind counts, the R58 withdrawal, the 25/25 result, and all four gap descriptions.

## ERRATUM — three matrix rows corrected against their source (found during Step 3)

The approved matrix's rows for R34, R36 and R37 do not match the
Round 7 register (PROCESS-TREE-D3-REVIEW-RESPONSE-v0.7.md), which
is the findings' source of record. The matrix rows described a
bearer/actor distinction (R34), an A-3 acceptance re-siting (R36)
and an A-4 role-claim discipline (R37) — none of which is the
register's finding under those IDs. The register's actual
findings: R34 — REQ-A-1's unconditional triggering-event link;
R36 — REQ-K-3's "instance-free (e.g. CREATION at binding)"
example contradicting the creation model; R37 — REQ-K-3's
multi-instance CREATION ordering underspecified. The error was
Remmy's: the rows were consolidated from compressed daily-log
summaries instead of the register's verbatim text (the matrix

## Blueprint Stage 5 — Canonicalisation, evaluation identity, defect links (R35, R48, R53, R55, R38)

  parse layer (register's correction, both halves).** (a) The
  headline claim "EXACT content — exactly as authored, code point
  for code point" is retired: the procedure now claims byte-exact
  identity over the canonical serialisation, strings and keys
  unnormalised, numbers and member order canonical by scheme,
  and states it is NOT a digest over the entries exactly as
  authored. (b) Duplicate exact keys: rejected by the record
  parser, recursively at every object level, before

  record structures; canonicalisation's loud failure is retained
  as backstop, not mechanism. Status: implemented.

  excludes exactly the content-identity fields (the digest value
  itself; any covered field whose value is that digest or one
  derived from it), per entry, over every covered entry, and
  nothing else: entry identities, ordering positions and all
  content fields are covered; the default for any unlisted field
  is COVERED; excluding more changes the procedure and forfeits
  the identifier. Status: implemented.

  record cites at issuance the record identity (iii), the
  consumed-reference identity (iv) and the coverage point it
  folded; the evaluator consumes exactly that record as an
  identity-bound snapshot; a presented record differing in
  contents, ordering or coverage fails verification against the
  identified record — never a silent re-target; a modified
  stream invalidates verification rather than changing the
  evaluation's basis. Checked against R48 at the same site:
  verification re-derives (vi) under R48's boundary, so a
  differing record mismatches by construction. Status:
  implemented.

  now specified as a separate identity-bearing addition under
  C-3 (vi)'s append lineage: own identity, new content identity
  citing its predecessor, links verdict → ruling; the original
  verdict's content and identity unchanged; reports show both
  the original and the annotation, never the annotation in
  place of the original. Status: implemented.
- **R38 — REQ-H-6 LINK entries (Alex's mechanism, from the
  register).** New appended entry kind: LINK — names the defect
  identity, the linked instance/evaluation identity, and the
  link kind; later-created affected evaluations link in without
  mutating the creation entry; H-4's reciprocity is the pair
  (evaluation's citation + the LINK entry). Acceptance fixture
  (v) added. R58 remains folded into R38 — not separately
  implemented. Status: implemented.

  LINK entries; C-3 (vi)'s append-lineage language and R55's
  annotation agree (new content identity, predecessor cited).

D3 v0.8 — STAGE 6 FIXTURE RESULTS (Revision 3 — two corrections) > The corrections, point by point

## The corrections, point by point

1. FX-R40e (was tautological) — REPLACED. A classification
   procedure (classify_instance) now runs over real inputs:
   an instance created by rule instantiation with a bearer
   classifies "assigned: <bearer>"; an instance whose input
   OMITS the bearer key entirely — {"origin":
   "rule-instantiation"} — classifies "machinery defect" — the
   classification is derived from the input by the procedure,

## Round 1 — first window (Alex), letter batches, 2026-11-09 [reported]

Source letters: pb-mwadwjve, pb-mwadylpb, pb-mwae0mjt, pb-mwae71m1 (review), pb-mwaeo0nm (disposition).

Specification-level assessments: R42 textually addressed — the revised REQ-B-1/REQ-K-1 wording removes the identified contradiction (B-1's binding-time refusal unconditional; K-1 the proposed instrument); both requirements remain PROPOSED; final R42 disposition withheld pending harness inspection. C-1's boundary (creating trigger authorises and counts, establishes nothing) and C-2's INDETERMINATE path identified as R47's decisive tests. C-2's eligibility machinery depends on B-1's proposed mandatory declaration (D3-R21); the dependency must remain conditional. E-6/I-2/K-3/K-4 mapped: role separation must be structural; R60 must not be represented as proof of checker independence (UX-1 open); K-3's taxonomy is itself PROPOSED (fixtures show internal consistency, not promotion); K-4's five provenance relationships must each be tested independently.

Disposition for harness batches 5–6: **PARTIAL PASS** (pb-mwaeo0nm), with six findings:

1. FX-R40b manually constructs the conditional CREATION entry — asserted, not generated by the mechanism under test.
2. FX-R47b is useful: qualifying trigger content contrasted with admitted determinations; the channel distinction is meaningfully tested.
3. FX-R63a provenance problem: bind() generates unconditional CREATION entries at binding; the fixture re-presents them as creations produced after a trigger — different causal mechanisms. The validator also never checks the entries belong to the named trigger.
4. validate_stream_identity() does not itself enforce the CREATION-instance requirement: a CREATION entry marked instance_free_declared=True could pass it, contrary to R63's stated contract.
5. FX-R44 demonstrates the reverse mixed channel without a synthetic event. Good.
6. FX-R52's closure string is derived by the test from the returned state, not demonstrated from closure machinery.

Standing instruction from that round: these are verification gaps, not automatic proof the requirements or implementation are wrong; the distinction between a passing fixture, a tested mechanism, and a demonstrated end-to-end property must be kept.

9. R65 — all five relationships receive mismatch tests, but the validator compares reference strings against expected values; it does not independently establish that the referenced underlying records are authentic.

C-1's quantified-trigger case (trigger count 1 while NOT_STARTED) is particularly important. D-3's terminal race is intentional chronology, not contradiction; artefact availability under PROGRESS: NONE (locking SATISFIED before the first entry folds) and post-lock auditability are the critical implementation checks. K-1's whole-binding failure is the consequential proposed clause; what "checked" means for judgement-based conditions remains unsettled (UX-4) and fixtures cannot settle it. ## Round 2 — continuation (Alex, second window), 2026-11-09 [reported]

Source letter: pb-mwag3pk0.

Correction acceptance: the examiner accepted Remmy's canonical-text correction in full and withdrew the earlier canonical-text concern entirely — the masked strings were introduced by the rendering/transcription pipeline, not the specification or harness; no canonicalization defect arises from them. The exam-pack framing sentence is a separate record-accuracy issue; the verified pack hash is not treated as evidence the pack is free of that known transcription error. No republication was necessary for the examination to proceed (the corrected edition snap-v09-exam2 was nevertheless published and stands); the correction remains attached to the examination record.

Implementation cluster 1 (fold engine + FX-R44) — observations:

- Channel (ii) determinations are admitted at the start only when admitted_basis_ok is true; non-admitted determinations are retained separately. Noted: admission is represented by a supplied boolean — the fixture does not establish that the admission mechanism itself verifies preservation and eligibility.
- Channel (i) determinations are indexed by the position of their supporting event — consistent with D-3's availability rule.
- The engine processes blockers in stream order and prevents later determinations from changing a locked state.
- FX-R44 is a useful positive fixture (artefact progress + event satisfaction deriving SATISFIED with no synthetic entries), but its assertions cover the final state and stream length only.

**Suspected substantive D-3 implementation defect — RECORDED AS SUSPECTED, NOT FINAL:** the fold's advance() permits a direct NOT_STARTED → SATISFIED transition whenever SATISFACTION and PROGRESS are both in the running set (or PROGRESS is declared NONE), without checking D-3's stated conditions for the direct step (PROGRESS: NONE, or a single basis establishing both predicates, or the path through IN_PROGRESS). Satisfaction-first-then-progress-later therefore derives SATISFIED directly, and — against REQ-B-2's "derives SATISFIED through IN_PROGRESS" — no fixture assertion proves the intermediate state occurred (FX-R44 included: its expected final state is correct, but the assertion does not demonstrate the path). Requires the examiner's determination.

**Audit concern:** the fold returns predicate names in its running set but discards their channel and evidence-basis associations, which D-3 requires determinations to retain. Whether another component preserves those associations in the evaluation record is unestablished.

Implementation cluster 2 (FX-R47 + FX-R52) was delivered at the examiner's request after that letter; its examination is the next step. Clusters 3–5 remain held at the examiner's instruction.

Pack edition erratum (Remmy, 2026-11-09): edition snap-v09-exam2's specification parts were defective — an assembly error put garbled headings on them and omitted the section bodies entirely (heading and a character count only). The defect was found mechanically before any examiner used that edition: the first window worked from letters, the second from snap-v09-exam1 plus letters. Edition snap-v09-exam3 restored the bodies but its brief understated the defect ("bodies were unaffected"); edition snap-v09-exam4 carries this corrected statement. The harness, results, register and brief parts of exam2 were unaffected. No examination conclusion rests on exam2.

D3 v0.9 — Examination Findings Ledger > Independent assessment — Grok [reported, 2026-11-10 ~05:01 PST]

## Independent assessment — Grok [reported, 2026-11-10 ~05:01 PST]

Ben consulted Grok, whose report states it independently retrieved the forum's JSON endpoint (HTTP 200, full body, token and list confirmed) — a non-OpenAI AI fetcher reading the Funnel address without difficulty. Grok's diagnosis converges with Vane's eligibility hypothesis: "Cache miss" means the URL is absent from OpenAI's index/cache and the live-fetch path did not deliver a body; it does not prove a request reached the origin. Ranked causes: (1) hostname class — *.ts.net Funnel names are dynamic tunnel endpoints, handled differently from ordinary indexed domains like community.nodebb.org; (2) new hostname + restricted live path; (3) transient factors. Proposed controls: ordinary-public-domain copy of the same JSON; known-good vs new Funnel comparison; back-to-back community-vs-ours fetches with exact error text; GitHub Pages re-test after a delay (already planted as the discovery experiment). Bottom line in its words: origin working and guest-accessible; the failure sits in ChatGPT's retrieval handling of the Funnel hostname class. No production changes recommended.

embed_text:
D3 v0.10 — CHANGE RECORD > The three repairs > R47 — trigger-content admission test (FX-R47b; fold engine)

### R47 — trigger-content admission test (FX-R47b; fold engine)
**Defect (as adjudicated):** FX-R47b placed qualifying predicate content on a conditional trigger and asserted the fold established nothing from it — but the fold never read `content_predicates` (one occurrence in the harness, fixture data only). The case passed even if the content were deleted: it demonstrated absence of admission, not examination of the admission boundary.
**Repair:** `fold()` now examines trigger-carried content — it collects every entry's `content_predicates` and records them in its returned result as `examined_trigger_content`. Admission remains the only path into the running set; examined content is never admitted. FX-R47b now asserts three things in one case: (1) with qualifying content present, the fold's examination record shows the content was read (["PROGRESS", "SATISFACTION"]) and the outcome still establishes nothing; (2) mutation control — the same trigger with its content removed empties the examination record and changes no outcome; (3) channel control — the same predicates supplied as admitted determinations satisfy. The fixture now fails if the examination is removed, not merely if the outcome changes.

D3 v0.10 — CHANGE RECORD > The three repairs > R60 — checker contract (CheckerContract, validate_verdict, FX-R60a–e)

### R60 — checker contract (CheckerContract, validate_verdict, FX-R60a–e)
**Defect (as adjudicated):** the contract recorded a procedure name without executing or validating it, and the verdict omitted the implementation hash, so REQ-I-2's reproducibility trio (declared version, implementation hash, input artefact identities) was never established; rejection of an incomplete verdict was unexercised. The reference implementation itself did not satisfy the specified contract.
**Repair:** the validation procedure now exists as an executable function, `_preservation_check`, which recomputes the artefact payload's SHA-256 and compares it against the digest pinned in the contract; `CheckerContract.run()` executes it. Every verdict carries the full trio — version, procedure identity, input identity, and `implementation_hash` (SHA-256 of the procedure's own source, computed at run time). A new `validate_verdict()` accepts a verdict only when every element matches the contract, naming the specific defect on rejection. FX-R60b now exercises: genuine verdict accepted; forged procedure stamp rejected; implementation hash missing rejected; implementation hash altered rejected; input identity missing rejected; version missing rejected. FX-R60a/c/d/e are unchanged in substance and re-executed.

heading_path: DUENNA — SIMPLIFICATION AUDIT (PROPOSAL, v0.1) > 2. Alex's six questions, answered
embed_text:
DUENNA — SIMPLIFICATION AUDIT (PROPOSAL, v0.1) > 2. Alex's six questions, answered

## 2. Alex's six questions, answered

**Historical material — can revision history live in a separate change
record?** Yes, entirely, and it mostly already does: per-revision change
records exist for v0.8 (D3-V08-CHANGE-RECORD), v0.9 and v0.10. What remains
inside the spec is (a) §18–23 (≈200 lines) and (b) the inline archaeology
(78 mentions). Both are SAFE extractions (Proposals S-1, S-2). A side benefit
is correctness, not just brevity: this programme has already been bitten by
compressed restatements of settled rulings living inside normative text
(the J-1 compression that would have barred Ben himself from approving).
Normative text that states only the rule cannot drift from the record of
how the rule was reached, because the record lives in one place.

**Duplicate machinery — one implementation, several tests?** Yes, in at
least four places: the terminal-state rules are stated three times
(D-3's closed transition set, D-5, D-6); "transitions are computed, never
declared" is stated in B-2, D-2 and D-3; the binding's lack of discretion
is stated in A-2 and J-2; and the append-with-new-content-identity lineage
mechanism is specified three times (C-3 (vi), H-3's annotations, H-6's
LINK/disposition entries). Proposals M-1…M-6.

**Excessive record structures?** The record *kinds* are not excessive —
K-3's taxonomy is minimal and load-bearing. What is excessive is the
*number of places that re-specify the same record behaviours*: the stream/
register boundary is restated in K-3, D-7, G-1, H-3 and H-6; identity
duties are restated in C-3, D-7, H-6 and K-3. One statement per behaviour,
cited elsewhere (part of M-5/S-2). The defect record (H-6) is the one
genuinely heavy structure; see U-2.

**Validation layers — meaningful properties, or internal agreement?**
Mostly meaningful, with one honest exception the audit must name: REQ-K-4's
report-completeness validation checks that the report *contains* what the
other requirements produced — it validates the projection against its
sources, which is internal agreement by design. That is worth keeping
(it is how a silently dropped component is caught), but it should be
*classified* as a projection check, not counted as an independent
validation layer (Proposal M-7). The genuinely independent layers —
evaluator vs checker (I-2) vs examiner (E-6) — are protected and retained.

**Lifecycle complexity?** The state machine itself is already minimal:
four states, a closed transition set, terminal locking. Nothing to cut
without losing a distinction Alex named as protected. The simplification
available is presentational: D-3's derivation procedure is the whole
machine; D-5/D-6 merge into it (M-1), and the B-2/D-2/D-3 restatement
triangle collapses (M-2). Transitions and distinctions survive intact.

**Reporting as projection?** Yes — K-4 is already a compilation ("compiled
from Tree §1.5, §5, §7, §9" is its own source line). Proposal M-7 makes it
officially a projection schema: each report component is owned by its
source requirement; K-4 shrinks to the projection list plus its one real
rule (a report missing a component is incomplete as a report) and its
standing caveats (checker verdicts as REPORTED; the I-4 caveat verbatim).

embed_text:
DUENNA — SIMPLIFICATION AUDIT (PROPOSAL, v0.1) > 3. The five-piece decomposition — tested against the 48 requirements

## 3. The five-piece decomposition — tested against the 48 requirements

Alex's proposed decomposition: **Contract** (what must happen), **Ledger**
(what actually happened), **Evaluator** (what the evidence establishes),
**Authority gate** (what is permitted next), **Examiner** (can it be
independently verified). Every requirement was assigned a primary piece:

| Piece | Requirements (primary home) | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Contract | A-1, A-2 (+J-2), A-3, B-1, B-3, B-4, B-6, K-1, K-2* | 10 |
| Ledger | A-4, C-3, D-7, G-1, H-3, H-6, I-1, K-3 | 8 |
| Evaluator | A-5, A-6*, B-2, B-5*, C-1, C-2, D-1…D-6, E-1…E-5, F-1*, G-2, H-1, H-2, H-4 | 22 |
| Authority gate | J-1 (+H-7), H-5 | 3 |
| Examiner | E-6, I-2, I-3, I-4*, K-4 | 5 |

(* = straddles or register items, below.)

**Finding: the decomposition is viable.** The seams already exist in the
specification — the families map almost cleanly (A/B/K-1 → Contract;
C-3/K-3 and the register-resident parts of D/G/H → Ledger; D/E/F and the
attribution rules → Evaluator; J → Gate; I and E-6 → Examiner). Family K
is the exception that proves the reading: its own title ("pre-binding
controls and cross-cutting duties") admits it is four pieces wearing one
family letter, and under the decomposition it dissolves — K-1 to Contract,
K-2 to the register, K-3 to Ledger, K-4 to the Examiner's surface.

Honest straddles (a decomposition that hid these would be appearance):
- **A-6** — the enumeration artefact is Ledger; its acceptance is Evaluator.
- **K-1** — the check is Contract; its binding-failure effect is enforced
  at the Gate's side of binding (A-2 already states the total-failure rule).
- **I-3** — preservation-failure semantics govern checker verdicts
  (Examiner) and are consumed as evaluation status (Evaluator).
- **C-3** — fold ordering (a) is Evaluator; identities and canonicalisation
  (b)–(f) are Ledger. See Proposal S-3.
- **K-4** — a projection over Ledger + Evaluator outputs, read by the
  Examiner.

Interfaces between pieces are already the design's spine: pieces
communicate by *cited identities* (C-3), never by shared mutable state.
The reduced architecture in §5 keeps exactly that.

DUENNA — SIMPLIFICATION AUDIT (PROPOSAL, v0.1) > 4. Proposals > SAFE — structural, no behavioural change

### SAFE — structural, no behavioural change

**S-1. Extract §18–23 (in-spec change records, ≈200 lines) to the
change-record series.** What disappears from the spec: nothing normative —
the six records are history, already preserved as the v0.1…v0.7 files they
describe; the spec keeps a three-line pointer and the hash chain stays in
the evidence ledger. No requirement depends on §18–23 (no requirement body
cites them). Guarantee preserved by: the change records themselves, which
is where v0.8–v0.10 history already lives.

**S-2. Extract inline revision archaeology (78 mentions) to the change
record.** Each requirement keeps its normative text plus at most a pointer
("history: change record, R##"). Behaviour identical — corrections changed
text in the past; the *current* text is what binds, and it is preserved
verbatim. Largest wins: B-2, C-3, D-3, K-1, K-3, H-6. Risk named plainly:
pointers must be exact, or the fidelity problem moves rather than dies;
the extraction is mechanical and diff-verifiable (the normative sentences
survive byte-identical, in order).

**S-3. Split REQ-C-3 into its two natural requirements, and cite
D3-CANON-1 as an external procedure.** C-3 (139 lines) is five mechanisms
under one ID: fold ordering; the identity taxonomy (i)–(iv);
evaluation-record identity (v); content identity + append lineage (vi);
the CANON-1 canonicalisation procedure; consumption binding. Proposal:
C-3 keeps fold ordering + the taxonomy; (v)+(vi) become the Ledger's
record-identity requirement; CANON-1's text moves — byte-identical — to a
separately versioned procedure document cited by identifier (the spec
already treats it that way: "An implementation that excludes any other
path… must not cite this identifier"). Provenance is not reduced: the
procedure text, the R49 canonicalisation fixtures, and the digest duties
are unchanged; only the address changes. Equivalence evidence: the R49
fixture family exercises CANON-1 directly and must pass unchanged against
the relocated text. Classification SAFE for the relocation, with the
excluded-paths *design* itself flagged separately as U-1.

### REMOVE — bodies whose function survives elsewhere

**R-1. REQ-K-2's body is removed; the question stays in the register.**
What disappears: an 11-line requirement whose entire content is an
absence (no clock semantics defined; none may be invented). Why
unnecessary as a *requirement*: its prohibition is the specification's
global stance ("no gap is filled by assumption"; semantics arrive only
by contract revision under J-1), and its acceptance is not a fixture but
a conformance scan of the spec text. Surviving guarantee: UX-2 remains
in the UNRESOLVED register verbatim; the no-invention clause is stated
once in the reduced Contract piece; the conformance scan survives as a
spec-level check. Dependents: K-2's pointer to J-1 (future clocks arrive
by revision) is preserved in the register entry. **The owner question —
should any obligation carry a clock — is NOT settled by this removal and
remains open exactly as before.**

**R-2. REQ-I-4's body is removed; UX-1 stays in the register, and the
PROPOSED minimum property moves into I-2.** What disappears: a 16-line
body whose content is "UNRESOLVED, plus a proposed minimum property."
Why unnecessary as a standalone body: everything it protects is carried
by (a) UX-1 in the register, (b) K-4's standing caveat in every report
("checker independence is UNRESOLVED"), and (c) I-2's own text ("a hash
is not independence, and U4 remains unresolved"). The minimum property —
a checker must be able to fail when the checked component fails in the
way the checker exists to catch — is a real proposed rule about
checkers, so it moves into I-2 as a PROPOSED clause, where it binds the
thing it describes. Surviving tests: I-4 has no fixtures by design
(acceptance class NOT-YET); nothing testable is lost. Dependents: I-2's
reference to I-4 retargets to UX-1. **Checker independence itself is
protected and is NOT removed, weakened or settled — only its mailing
address changes.**

### UNRESOLVED — owner/design decisions the audit surfaces, not settles

**U-1. D3-CANON-1's excluded paths.** The content identity excludes
three field paths by name (R48's design); an exception list must be
maintained forever, and its boundary fixture is one of the four open
gaps. Alternative shape: cover everything, and carry lineage entirely
in the structurally separate citation envelope (which already exists).
Deciding this is a design decision with provenance consequences — it is
flagged, not proposed.

**U-2. H-6's LINK-entry reciprocity machinery.** Reciprocity itself is
provenance and protected. The *mechanism* — a third entry kind whose
sole job is linking, with reciprocity specified for both creation
orders — is the heaviest machinery in the spec relative to the frequency
of its event (defects are rare; runs are many). A simpler mechanism
(link at creation; later evaluations linked from the evaluation side
under the shared append lineage, M-5) may preserve the guarantee with
one entry kind fewer. The (v)/(vi) fixtures are owed under either
mechanism; choosing is a design decision.

**U-3. Whether Family E's five requirements become one evaluation-record
schema.** E-1/E-3/E-4/E-5 already describe one record from four sides.
A single schema requirement with four acceptance groups would match the
implementation reality; but the axes/findings distinctions are semantic
and load-bearing, and merging text risks exactly the compression failures
this programme has recorded before. Flagged for the design process, with
the fixture-mapping table (§6) as the safety instrument if it proceeds.

## 5. The proposed reduced architecture

Five pieces, interfaces by cited identity only:

1. **Contract** — pinned rule anatomy (B-1), binding (A-1, A-2), the
   pre-binding satisfiability check (K-1). *Emits:* the contract instance.
2. **Ledger** — the stream and its taxonomy (K-3), identities and
   canonicalisation (C-3 split per S-3, CANON-1 cited), preservation
   duties (I-1), and the registers: rule ledger (A-4), discharge (G-1),
   defect records (H-6), annotations (H-3). *Emits:* the closed record,
   cited by identity.
3. **Evaluator** — channels (B-2), window (C-1, C-2), derivation (D-1,
   D-3, D-4, D-7), evaluation (E-1, E-3, E-4, E-5), attribution (H-1,
   H-2, H-4), closure (G-2, F-1's clauses). *Emits:* the evaluation
   record, citing the record it consumed.
4. **Authority gate** — approval (J-1), defect-discharge effect (H-5),
   evidence receipt (E-6's gate role). *Emits:* permissions for what
   happens next; owns no evaluation.
5. **Examiner** — three-way separation (E-6), checker contracts (I-2,
   I-3), the report projection (K-4). *Emits:* verdicts on support,
   carried as REPORTED evidence with the independence caveat.

**every acceptance fixture retained** under its surviving requirement.

and de-duplicating the restatements, yields an estimated normative
document of roughly **950–1,050 lines** (estimate, labelled as such —
the exact figure is knowable only by doing the extraction under the
equivalence procedure, §6).

## 6. Equivalence — how any of this would be proven before it is adopted

No proposal above changes normative text by this document's say-so.
Equivalence procedure, in order:

1. **Fixture-mapping table first.** Every acceptance fixture named in
   the current specification is listed against its home in the reduced
   architecture. A fixture with no home stops the process. (Honest
   caveat: the 31-case harness covers the correction-matrix findings;
   several spec-named acceptance fixtures have never been implemented.
   The mapping table must mark which fixtures exist as code and which
   exist only as spec text — the audit does not claim a coverage the
   record does not show.)
2. **Mechanical extraction, diff-verified.** S-1/S-2 are performed as
   text moves; a diff proves the normative sentences survive verbatim.
3. **The harness re-runs against the reduced text's requirements** —
   same 31 cases, same expected outcomes; sabotage discipline retained
   (a merge that cannot be made to fail by removing its mechanism is
   appearance, not equivalence).
4. **Independent examination of the equivalence claim itself** — the
   Claude/Vane pattern — before adjudication. OWNER-RULED text (J-1,
   H-5) is never merged by anyone's authority but Ben's; M-4 is
   conditional on his ruling.
5. Only then: a simplified revision is opened as its own versioned
   step, under the same gates as v0.9 and v0.10.

embed_text:
DUENNA — STEP 3: REQUIREMENT → FUNCTION MAPPING AND DEPENDENCY EXTRACTION > Dependency extraction

## Dependency extraction

Function-level dependencies (X → Y reads "Y cannot operate without X"):

- **F1 → F2:** instances exist to be recorded; the Ledger's entries cite
  contract instances and their CREATION points.
- **F2 → F3:** derivation folds the record; no record, no fold (E-5 is the
  failure-shaped proof: derivation degrades exactly where the record does).
- **F3 → F4:** accounting reads derived states (discharge forms, findings,
  closure outcomes are all functions of the fold's results).
- **F2 + F3 + F4 → F6:** re-derivation replays the record through the
  derivation and compares accounts; its machinery (identities, digests,
  consumption binding) exists to make that replay exact.
- **F5 ⊥ all:** authority touches no stage's operation; it governs
  *change to the rules of every stage* (J-1) and the effect of findings
  that require contract revision (H-5). It is orthogonal by design —
  that orthogonality IS the externally enforceable boundary.

The graph is therefore a **chain, not a mesh**: F1 → F2 → F3 → F4 → F6,
with F5 around it. Per Alex's ruling that functions and dependencies set
the component count, the shape this suggests is a four-stage pipeline
(bind → record → derive/account → verify) under an authority shell —
whether "derive" and "account" are one stage or two is the F3/F4
question, next.

Requirement-level hubs (mechanical extraction): K-3 cites 12
requirements, K-4 cites 13 (a projection — its citation count is its
job), K-1 cites 6, C-3 is cited by 6. No substantive cycles: every
citation cycle in the graph is definitional (e.g. C-1 ↔ K-3 on the
creation point), not operational.

heading_path: DUENNA — STEP 3: REQUIREMENT → FUNCTION MAPPING AND DEPENDENCY EXTRACTION > The three investigations — Remmy's positions, for challenge
embed_text:
DUENNA — STEP 3: REQUIREMENT → FUNCTION MAPPING AND DEPENDENCY EXTRACTION > The three investigations — Remmy's positions, for challenge

## The three investigations — Remmy's positions, for challenge

**(a) F3 + F4: one mechanism, two guarantee-sets.** The fold produces
one derivation; accounting is computed from that derivation plus the
record — there is no second engine in the current design, and none is
needed. But the guarantees are not the same guarantee. F3's tests prove
states are never declared or unearned (transition discipline). F4's
tests prove the account is *complete*: D-7 is the counterexample to
full merger — a fold can be perfectly lawful while an unmet, unblocked
instance passes unrecorded, because nothing in the derivation
*obliges* the report to surface it. Accounting is the completeness
projection over the derivation; derivation is the state engine.
One mechanism, two acceptance families — Alex's own distinction
(guarantees vs mechanisms) applied to his question. Proposed: **one
stage, two guarantee-sets, separately tested.**

**(b) F2: the minimal machinery for "cannot silently change."** The
guarantee decomposes into three needs: *name* what changed (stable
identities), *prove* what changed (a content digest), *correct* without
erasing (append-only additions). The current design's identities +
digest + append lineage meet exactly those three. **D3-CANON-1 exceeds
them**: canonicalisation is not needed to detect change in a record you
hold; it is needed when an independent party must reproduce the same
digest from a differently serialised copy — which is F6's work, not
F2's. Position: CANON-1 should be justified (and sized) as F6
machinery. The six-part identity taxonomy also exceeds F2: (ii) is
admitted in-text to be a special case of (i); (iv) consumed-reference
identity is F6 machinery (re-derivation must know exactly what was
folded). Minimal F2 = entry identity, record content digest,
append-only registers. The rest is F6, honestly labelled.

**(c) F5: authority, precisely.** Three different things must not be
conflated: Ben's approval of *normative change* (J-1 — his alone,
protected); *delegated execution* (Alex's three calls; Remmy's in-loop
steps — intact, and not per-action approvals); and *machinery effects*
(binding totals, K-1 refusals, fold outcomes — automatic consequences
of approved rules, which are not authority acts at all). The failure
mode to police is a machinery effect quietly becoming a discretion —
which is exactly what A-2's purity and K-1's "the refusal is B-1's,
not this check's grant" already guard. Position: F5 needs J-1 plus the
no-discretion clauses, and nothing else; any proposal that adds an
approval step inside a run has misunderstood the function.

## Part 2 — F5: authority edges (response to Alex's strongest objection)

Alex's objection is sustained in part, and the mapping's claim is
corrected: F5 is not a shell with no edges. The precise model, with the
distinction that keeps enforcement from becoming discretion:

- **Governance edges (external, change what the pipeline runs on):**
  contract approval (J-1 → the rule-set F1 binds); supersession rulings
  (J-1 / H-3 → appended to the record, never edits). Decisions originate
  outside the machinery, always.
- **Enforcement edges (mechanical checks at pipeline points, verifying a
  permission state that is pinned in an approved artefact):** A-2 binds
  only an approved, version-pinned contract — approval is checked *as
  data* at F1's door; H-5's defect-discharge takes effect only when the
  pinned contract version contains the A1 revision — a version check,
  not a judgement; the E-6 gate judges evidence receipt against
  contract-set criteria before downstream stages rely on a result.
- **No decision edges:** no stage originates a permission, an approval
  or a waiver. Where a check fails, the machinery stops or refuses
  (fail-closed); it never substitutes its own permission.

Alex's three questions, answered in the model's terms: *Who may
establish or change a binding rule?* Ben, by J-1 — a governance edge.
*Who may initiate an instance?* No one's discretion: binding and record
events initiate mechanically; the authority was exercised upstream, in
approving the contract that defines the triggers. *What
determines whether downstream execution may proceed following a
verified result?* The gate evaluates evidence receipt against the
criteria established by the approved contract (E-6). The contract
defines the consequence of that result; the machinery applies it.
The gate originates no permission. (Question and answer corrected to
Alex's replacement wording on his verification of this document,
2026-11-10 — the original phrasing framed the gate as permitting,
the ambiguity retired in Part 2's model.)

Adopted formulation: **F5 is externally governed, mechanically enforced
authority** (Alex's words), with governance and enforcement edges drawn
explicitly in the dependency graph and decision edges absent by
construction. The mapping document's "orthogonal" is corrected to:
*orthogonal in decision, connected in enforcement.*

DUENNA — STEP 4 EXAMINATION MATERIAL (duplicates · F5 edges · correction destinations) > Part 3 — Correction destinations (U-2 under F2), incl. LINK entries

## Part 3 — Correction destinations (U-2 under F2), incl. LINK entries

Alex's reframing accepted: the question is whether every record
category has a lawful correction destination — a place a correction can
land without mutating history. Inventory from the specification:

| Record category | Correction destination | State |
|---|---|---|
| Execution-stream entries | None — by design. A wrong entry is answered by later entries and report flagging (UNCLASSIFIED, unmapped-event lines); it is never edited | Deliberate; sufficiency worth one explicit confirmation at step 4 |
| Evaluation records | H-3 dispute annotations + C-3 (vi) append lineage (new content identity citing predecessor) | Lawful destination exists |
| Defect records | Their own append kinds: disposition entries, LINK entries | Exists — but see LINK note |
| Checker verdicts | **None specified.** I-2/I-3 govern verdict content and failure semantics; nothing states how a verdict later shown wrong is superseded or annotated | **GAP — tabled, not filled** |
| Discharge records | None specified directly; arguably inherits the evaluation record's annotation path, since discharge lives in the evaluation register (G-1/K-3) | Ambiguous — flag for step 4 |
| Owner rulings | Versioned decisions supersede (H-3 / J-1) | Exists |

**On LINK entries specifically:** the LINK kind exists because a defect
record must be able to *acquire* links after creation (an affected
evaluation may not exist yet when the defect is found). It is, in
effect, the defect record's home-grown correction/growth destination —
invented locally for one record category, in parallel with the general
append lineage C-3 (vi) already provides for evaluation records. Under
one shared append mechanism, LINK becomes a *use* of the mechanism (an
append entry of link kind) rather than a separately specified machinery.
The reciprocity guarantee is untouched by that reframing; only its
machinery count changes. The H-6 (v)/(vi) fixtures remain owed either
way — this examination does not close them.

**The inventory's real finding is the checker-verdict gap:** the one
record category with verdicts other components rely on (K-4 carries
them; evaluations may rely on them visibly, D3-R12) has no specified
way to mark a verdict superseded. Recorded here as a finding for the
joint process. Per the working principles — no new safeguards by
default — this document proposes no mechanism for it; it names the
hole and leaves its disposition to steps 4–6.

## Part 4 — C-3: cross-functional requirement vs implementation dependency

Alex's distinction is accepted and the audit's S-3 is refined by it:
that C-3 carries three functions does **not** by itself require three
requirement IDs. A single requirement may impose several independently
testable obligations. The implementation may still be built in three
pieces (identity store; digest/canonicalisation; fold order is the
Evaluator's in any case) without the *requirement* being split.
Refined proposal: C-3 remains one requirement; its obligations are
*grouped and labelled by function* (F2 identities / F6 re-derivation /
F3 fold order) so the seams are visible to implementers and examiners,
and CANON-1 is cited by identifier (its text byte-identical wherever
it lives). Split only if the grouping proves unworkable in the
implementation plan — a step-6 question, not a step-3 conclusion.

heading_path: DUENNA — STEP 6: THE SMALLEST VIABLE ARCHITECTURE > The four components
embed_text:
DUENNA — STEP 6: THE SMALLEST VIABLE ARCHITECTURE > The four components

## The four components

**RECORD — discharges F2.** Preserves original content whole, with
stable identity and content digest, append-only: nothing is
silently rewritten, ever. The record is the foundation — it does
not depend on binding, so evidence of a failed or absent binding is
recordable in it (the F1→F2 split from step 3). The identity
taxonomy stays PROVISIONAL inside this component: kinds are data,
not structure, and each kind still owes a distinct failure case or
it consolidates. Implementation may separate identity storage,
canonicalisation and digest machinery inside the component; those
are its internals, not new components.

**BINDER — discharges F1.** Binds authored rules into instances of
a pinned, approved contract — mechanically, with no discretion at
binding. BINDER outputs only to the RECORD: successful binding
produces instance entries; binding failure produces an explicit
failure entry. It has no other output channel. The absence of an
instance must not read as success (your step-4 test, carried here
as this component's acceptance shape).

**EVALUATOR — discharges F3 and F4, as ONE component with TWO
independently testable guarantee sets.** One mechanism: the fold
derives lifecycle states from evidence only (F3), and accounting
states every obligation satisfied, blocked, unmet or indeterminate
with attribution that cannot be relabelled (F4). The machinery is
shared; the guarantees are not merged — F3 and F4 keep separate
acceptance suites, and a pass in one suite says nothing about the
other. The append-only preservation and identity discipline is
owned by the RECORD. The EVALUATOR uses that discipline to append
evaluation annotations, defect dispositions and LINK entries —
append kinds of one mechanism, not three; the kinds and their
semantics remain defined by their respective requirements. The
Evaluator can produce entries; it cannot decide that history may
be rewritten. LINK's equivalence on that shared mechanism remains
UNPROVEN pending the H-6 (v)/(vi) fixtures — the architecture
carries that as a condition, not a claim.

**EXAMINER SURFACE — discharges F6.** In your wording, adopted:
"The Examiner independently re-derives from the preserved original
record, using the applicable pinned contract and defined
reproduction rules, without relying on the Evaluator's derived
state or conclusions." Reports (the K-4 material) are projections
produced through this surface, not a component of their own. The
Examiner's independent derivation uses the preserved original
record, the applicable pinned contract and the defined
reproduction rules; any additional report material — registers,
verdicts, defect records and other evidence carried outside the
stream — must be obtained through its specified evidence path and
must not be inferred from the Evaluator's conclusions. No
component grades its own work: the surface reads the RECORD and
the pinned contract, never the EVALUATOR's state.

**F5 is not a component.** It is two kinds of edge crossing every
component: governance edges — external, Ben's, the only place
authority originates — and enforcement edges — mechanical checks
against pinned approved artefacts at entry and progression points.
There are no decision edges. No gate, evaluator or examiner
invents a permission; the gate evaluates evidence receipt, the
approved contract defines the consequence, the machinery applies
it.

DUENNA — STEP 6: THE SMALLEST VIABLE ARCHITECTURE > Dependency statement

## Dependency statement

RECORD depends on nothing. BINDER depends on RECORD. EVALUATOR
depends on RECORD, consuming BINDER's recorded instance entries
through it — the record is the shared boundary between components.
EXAMINER SURFACE depends on RECORD, the pinned contract and the
reproduction rules — never on EVALUATOR outputs. Enforcement edges
cross all four; governance edges touch the whole from outside.
This is the amended chain from step 3, with its F1→F2 split
preserved: remove BINDER and the system still records; remove
RECORD and nothing else stands.

## Stage 1 — The five consolidations, one at a time

Executed in risk order, each as its own change with its own record,
under the execution rule: every retired body leaves a tombstone
(historical ID, never reused), a clause-level inventory of where
every part went, and its guarantee re-proven by running the fixture
against the survivor.

   not only validate the state set internally.

   machinery defect produces no F4 disposition.

   tombstone (D-3 for the body, G-2/F-1 for the sentence).

fixture that depends on that guarantee fail, while unrelated
fixtures remain unaffected, and the evidence identifies the
failures attributable to the disabled guarantee. A merge that
cannot pass its sabotage check is not complete, whatever the
green suite says.

  stating the problem, the binding constraints (original content

  verdict preserved, later finding recorded, operative verdict

  register as a NAMED OPEN ITEM, in those words. Not briefed, not
  solved, not inherited away.

  shared append mechanism, or the item stays UNPROVEN in the
  register — the plan records the dependency honestly: those

  register C-1), and this stage does not presume it.

who has authority to decide the disposition, and who implements an
authorised decision. Candidate shapes in a brief are UNRULED; a
brief cannot turn them into approved machinery. (Ben's delegation
to Remmy governs pending decisions inside the planning loop; it
does not transfer Ben's reserved owner authority over the
specification or the proposal's adoption.)

named; the register carries every unresolved item by name; nothing
in the proposal text resolves a carried item by implication.

# CLAUDE — VERIFICATION REPORT, D3 v0.10 RE-EXAMINATION

*Saved verbatim from Ben's relay of Claude's window, 2026-11-10
(~15:08 PST). Claude pulled the evidence himself from
github.com/Q420/ainternet-shelf (clone at commit 9b97219a) under
the pull letter (CLAUDE-PULL-LETTER-V010-REEXAMINATION.md). This
file is the relayed text as received, including his working
narration; the dispositions are in the structured report at the
end.*

---

I'll pull the v0.10 evidence from the shelf repository, starting with a fresh clone.

The `gh` clone failed because this session doesn't allow GraphQL. I'll attach the repository through the session's repo tool instead.

The repository is cloned. Next I'll check the file hashes against the MANIFEST and the hashes given in the letter.

The hash prefixes match the letter. I'll now check every MANIFEST entry against the files in the clone, not just the ones I was asked about.

All 59 MANIFEST entries match their files. Next I'll diff the v0.10 spec against the v0.9 seed, since the letter claims everything from "Source of record:" onward is identical.

The diff output looks cut off after the header. I'll print the full remainder to check whether anything changed past the header.

Only the header differs. The spec body from "Source of record:" onward is byte-identical to the v0.9 seed. Next I'll re-run the v0.10 harness in an isolated copy and compare its output with the delivered results.

The re-run matches the delivered results, and all 31 fixture IDs are the same as in v0.9. Next I'll read the R47, R60, and R65 mechanisms in the v0.10 harness.

The R47 mechanism now reads trigger content. The fold records it, and the mutation control shows the record changes when content is removed. But the content never affects the outcome, so the "content fails" variant is covered only by that same invariant, not by a fixture of its own. Next, R65 and R60.

The R60 trio and its rejection checks look real. However, the corrupted-payload fixture (FX-R60d) fails through a `corrupt` flag the artefact sets itself, before the digest comparison runs. I'll check whether any fixture reaches the digest-mismatch branch, and whether R61 uses the same procedure.

No fixture sends a mismatched payload into `CheckerContract.run` without the `corrupt` flag, so the digest-mismatch branch is never exercised. FX-R61 also tests its own copy of the logic, not `_preservation_check`. I'll test this directly by running sabotaged copies of the harness.

Sabotage results: removing the digest comparison (S1) went undetected, so the executable preservation check's rejection path is not tested. The other four sabotages each fail their own fixture. Next I'll read the v0.10 change record and the unresolved-items record, then check the regression conditions.

# VANE — INDEPENDENT EXAMINATION REPORT, D3 v0.10

*Saved verbatim from Vane's bridge message pb-mwbee83z-2-4o7s,
2026-11-10 (~15:46 PST). Vane pulled the evidence himself from
github.com/Q420/ainternet-shelf through his own GitHub connection
and states he deliberately did not consult Claude's report.*

---

Vane — independent examination of D3 v0.10

PB-ID: pb-20261110-vane-v010-independent-examination

Repository: Q420/ainternet-shelf
Specification: D3 v0.10
Examination basis: specification, change record, harness source and fixture results retrieved independently through GitHub.

1. R47 — Trigger-content admission

PASS

The repaired fold now actually reads trigger-carried content_predicates and records the examined content separately from admitted determinations.

FX-R47b is materially stronger than its v0.9 predecessor:

Qualifying content is present and demonstrably examined.

Removing that content empties the examination record.

Neither conditional trigger establishes progress or satisfaction.

Supplying the same predicates through the admitted-determination channel does satisfy.

The distinction between examination and admission is preserved.

I accept this repair.

2. R60 — Checker contract

FAIL — residual defect

The implementation has made substantial progress. It now executes _preservation_check, computes an implementation hash, records the input identity and version, and rejects incomplete or mismatched verdict metadata.

However, one important binding remains unenforced.

CheckerContract.__init__() accepts an arbitrary procedure identifier. run() always executes _preservation_check, regardless of that identifier.

Consequently, a contract can declare a fictitious procedure name, execute the preservation checker anyway, stamp the verdict with that fictitious name, and subsequently pass validate_verdict().

The validator compares the verdict's procedure string against the contract's procedure string, but neither is independently bound to the callable actually executed.

This is a different failure from the v0.9 forged-verdict problem. The repaired fixture tests whether a verdict can misrepresent its contract. It does not test whether the contract itself can misrepresent its executed procedure.

Required correction: bind the declared procedure identity to the actual executable validation procedure. Reject an unrecognised or mismatched identity rather than allowing arbitrary strings.

The implementation hash must identify that bound procedure.

I do not accept R60 as fully repaired.

3. R65 — Provenance completeness

PASS, within the authorised five-relationship scope

The repaired validator now checks:

Missing references.

Unexpected references.

Incorrect reference values.

Disagreement between components_present and the required set.

The formerly passing empty-reference case.

The deletion tests are particularly important. They demonstrate that completeness is tested, not merely the correctness of whatever happens to be supplied.

One boundary worth recording: the validator receives its required target set as an argument. The fixture supplies the correct five-element set, so the fixture demonstrates the intended behaviour for that set. It does not independently establish the authority of arbitrary target sets supplied by other callers.

This is a scope qualification, not a failure of the five targeted fixture cases.

I accept the authorised R65 repair.

4. Examination disposition

R47 — PASS

`PROCEDURE_REGISTRY` maps each claimable procedure identity to

the executed procedure; the verdict's `implementation_hash` is

a contract constructed with "fictitious procedure XYZ" is

sabotage-of-the-fixture runs for the v2.3 mechanisms (the
mutable-registry variant against FX-R60h under the factory, and
the restored-global-dispatch variant against FX-R60i) require
constructing deliberately weakened variants of the harness.

covers substitution through ordinary module-level attribute
assignment; it claims nothing against an actor who rewrites the
module's own functions or reaches into closure cells directly.

## Addendum 3 — Verdict provenance implemented (2026-11-10)

Alex authorised implementation of the revised FX-R60j/k
proposal (pb-mwbhu9zh), with his precision requirement: identity
by retained object references and `is` comparisons, not id()
integers. Implemented as harness **v2.4**:

- The factory closure holds a private **issuance record**. Each
  entry retains the actual contract instance, the actual
  verdict object it returned, and the fingerprint of the
  verdict's canonical contents at issuance.
- `validate_verdict` (after the existing field checks, which
  are unchanged and fire first) requires: an entry where
  `recorded contract is this contract` and `recorded verdict is
  this verdict` — else "REJECTED: verdict not issued by this
  contract" — and the current fingerprint equal to the issuance
  fingerprint — else "REJECTED: verdict altered after
  issuance".
- New fixtures **FX-R60j** (forgery with the genuine pinned
  hash rejected; genuine verdict accepted), **FX-R60k**
  (cross-contract replay rejected — different digest, and
  identical issued contents; same-contract control accepted),
  **FX-R60l** (issued object mutated after return rejected;
  genuine accepted).
- Full suite: **38 fixtures executed, 38 PASS, 0 FAIL** (31
  original identities + FX-R60f/g/h/i/j/k/l). Harness sha256
  **854a3e8644817ef1acb9c83be01a0164d3f987ada19e25fe972d86a7e0b2f9d5**;
  results sha256
  **902936d8aa27e6e75b48644cb2961f1ccbeeaa2344cf79c8573a77f9b470ad66**.

**Sabotage evidence:** the **integrity sabotage was executed
by the implementer** — with the fingerprint comparison removed,
**FX-R60l fails alone (37 PASS / 1 FAIL)**, the rest of the
suite unaffected. The **identity sabotage** (removing the
object-identity provenance check) could not be constructed by
the implementer — her tooling blocked the weakened variant
again — and is **assigned to independent examination**, with
the still-outstanding v2.3 sabotage runs (mutable-registry
variant vs FX-R60h under the factory; restored-global-dispatch
variant vs FX-R60i) and the executed reproduction of the v2.3
cross-contract replay (FX-R60k, established by inspection).
This record claims none of those as implementer-run.

Adjudicator: Alex, under Ben's delegation of 2026-11-08.
Summary of dispositions:

- **Correction A — PASS, ACCEPTED.** Claude's independent
  verification (all hashes, all 71 MANIFEST entries, isolated
  full-harness reproduction 34/34 identical) is substantially
  stronger evidence than the earlier targeted examination.

  rebinding is WITHIN Correction B's threat model. Rebinding
  defeats precisely the guarantee the protection exists for; it
  is a concrete, identifiable bypass, not the unreasonable claim
  that Python can resist arbitrary code execution with
  unrestricted internal access. The boundary must be explicit.
- **The mechanism problem, in Alex's words:** the implementation
  hash following the substitute callable means contract and
  validation agree with the same compromised source — **there is
  no independent trust anchor.**

- **Claude re-examination — ACCEPTED.**
- **Change-record housekeeping — corrected (commit abe6fab).**
- **v0.10 — NOT APPROVED.** No further implementation is
  authorised under the current revision.
- **Distinction preserved:** the R60 revision is NOT invalidated
  wholesale; its immutability guarantee is established as
  INCOMPLETE.

Required before another implementation: preserve both reports;
Correction A stays closed; Correction B stays open; define a
trusted registry reference that cannot be replaced through the
ordinary module-level dispatch path; ensure construction and
validation cannot establish trust merely by agreeing with the
same substituted implementation; add a dedicated module-rebinding
sabotage fixture; demonstrate the substitute cannot dispatch
successfully or validate as the original; re-run the complete
suite including both existing registry variants and the new
fixture. **The precise implementation is Remmy's to propose and
independent examination's to verify; the next step is a repair
PROPOSAL presented for review — not implementation.**

heading_path: R60 — REBIND REPAIR PROPOSAL (for Alex's review; NOT implementation) > Proposed mechanism — two parts, both needed
embed_text:
R60 — REBIND REPAIR PROPOSAL (for Alex's review; NOT implementation) > Proposed mechanism — two parts, both needed

## Proposed mechanism — two parts, both needed

**1. Dispatch from a captured reference, not the module global.**
The one true registry (a MappingProxyType over its single
entry) is created inside a factory scope and held in a closure.
`CheckerContract` is produced by that factory; construction
dispatches through the closure cell. The module-level name
`PROCEDURE_REGISTRY` may remain as a read-only display copy, but
nothing in the dispatch path reads it — rebinding it changes
nothing. (In Python terms: attribute assignment on the module
cannot reach a closure variable.)

**2. Validation against a pinned anchor, not the contract.**
At the same definition point, the canonical procedure's source
hash is computed once and pinned inside the protected scope.
`validate_verdict` accepts a verdict only if its
implementation_hash EQUALS the pinned hash for the claimed
identity. If a substitute ran — however it got dispatched — its
source hash differs and validation rejects the verdict. Trust no
longer comes from the contract agreeing with itself; it comes
from comparison against an anchor fixed before any contract
exists.

embed_text:
FX-R60J — FINDING AND REPAIR PROPOSAL (reported separately; NOT folded into the 35/35) > Proposed repair — verdict provenance via the issued-verdict record

## Proposed repair — verdict provenance via the issued-verdict record

The factory closure additionally holds an **issued-verdict
record**: every verdict dictionary `run()` returns is recorded
(its canonical serialisation) in a closure-held set before it
is returned. `validate_verdict()` gains one further check: the
submitted verdict must be **in the issued record** — the exact
verdict, whole and unaltered. A forged dictionary, however
perfect its fields, was never issued and is rejected:
`REJECTED: verdict not issued by this contract system`.

Why this mechanism: validation stops asking "does this
verdict *look* right?" and consults the record of what was
actually produced — the same RECORD-then-validate shape
Duenna's architecture specifies. Considered and held second: a
keyed seal (HMAC over the verdict, key in the closure) — sound,
but adds key handling to a fixture harness and proves only
"sealed by the keyholder," not "this run happened." The record
proves the run happened. (Both accept a verbatim replay of a
genuine verdict for the same input — correctly: that claim is
true and was issued.)

### Revised mechanism — issuance bound to the contract instance

The record becomes **per-contract**: the factory closure holds
a mapping from each contract instance to the set of verdicts
that instance has issued.

- Construction registers an empty issued-set for the new
  instance, keyed by the instance's identity (`id(self)` —
  object identity, which no attribute assignment can mint or
  move).
- `run()` records each verdict it returns in **its own
  contract's** set (canonical serialisation:
  `json.dumps(verdict, sort_keys=True)`).
- `validate_verdict()` requires membership in **the submitted
  contract's own set**: anything else —
  `REJECTED: verdict not issued by this contract`.

This closes FX-R60j (a fabrication is in no contract's set)
and FX-R60k (A's verdict is in A's set, not B's) with one
mechanism. Considered and rejected as weaker: an instance
identifier stamped into the verdict — a stamp is copyable, and
a copied stamp is exactly the FX-R60j lesson. Considered and
rejected as heavier: per-contract keyed seals — key handling
the record mechanism doesn't need. Stated caveat: `id()` keys
are an in-process identity; within a harness run, contracts
outlive their validation, and the append-only record makes a
recycled id harmless in practice (a new instance registers a
fresh empty set, overwriting nothing it could be confused
with — its own verdicts are recorded under its own live id).
Cross-process provenance remains out of scope, as before.

heading_path: FX-R60J — FINDING AND REPAIR PROPOSAL (reported separately; NOT folded into the 35/35) > Addendum 2 — Provenance refined to the issued OBJECT (Alex, pb-mwbhrtfa) > Revised mechanism — object identity + issuance fingerprint
embed_text:
FX-R60J — FINDING AND REPAIR PROPOSAL (reported separately; NOT folded into the 35/35) > Addendum 2 — Provenance refined to the issued OBJECT (Alex, pb-mwbhrtfa) > Revised mechanism — object identity + issuance fingerprint

### Revised mechanism — object identity + issuance fingerprint

The factory closure holds, per contract instance, a private
issuance record. When `run()` returns a verdict dictionary it
records, under the issuing contract's entry:

- the **identity of the returned object** (`id(verdict)`), and
- an **issuance fingerprint**: the hash of the verdict's
  canonical serialisation at the moment of issuance.

The record also **holds a reference to the object itself**, so
it cannot be garbage-collected and its identity cannot be
recycled while validation remains possible.

`validate_verdict(verdict, contract)` then requires **both**:

1. **Identity:** `id(verdict)` is present in *this contract's*
   issuance record — the exact object this contract issued.
2. **Integrity:** the fingerprint of the verdict's *current*
   contents equals the issuance fingerprint recorded for that
   object.

Consequences, case by case:

- **Genuine verdict, its own contract:** present, unaltered —
  ACCEPTED.
- **A's object offered to B (different digests):** not in B's
  record — REJECTED.
- **A's object offered to B where both issued identical
  contents:** B's record holds *B's* object's identity, not
  A's — REJECTED. (The serialisation-only design accepted
  this; that was the weakness.)
- **A copied dictionary, byte-for-byte identical:** a copy is
